items.title: Kano police recover car stolen from church at teaching hospital
items.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has recovered a Hyundai car stolen from a church in the state after tracing it to the premises of Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (AKTH). The vehicle, a golden-coloured Hyundai with registration number LAGOS AA 444 BL, was reportedly stolen on October 25, 2026, while its owner, Uchenna Emmanuel, was attending a church service at St. Thomas Church, Airport Road, Kano. The police said Emmanuel parked the vehicle within the church premises at about 11am but discovered it missing when he returned after the service. The Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Wednesday, saying operatives of the Command’s Special Intervention Squad (SIS) immediately launched an intelligence-led search following a report of the theft. According to him, the stolen vehicle was traced to Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital on October 26, where it was found parked within the premises. “The stolen vehicle was later found parked within the premises of Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital on October 26. Our operatives laid an ambush to arrest whoever brought it there, but nobody showed up to claim the vehicle,” Kiyawa said. He said the vehicle was eventually recovered on October 28 and taken to the SIS office for investigation before being handed over to its owner. Kiyawa added that Emmanuel commended the police for their prompt response and successful recovery of his vehicle. The police spokesman said the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, had advised motorists to install security devices, including vehicle trackers, steering locks and pedal locks, to protect their vehicles against theft. He also urged vehicle owners to ensure their cars were properly locked and secured, particularly when parked in public places such as churches, markets and hospitals. “Efforts are also ongoing to arrest the fleeing suspects, while investigation continues,” he said. The post Kano police recover car stolen from church at teaching hospital appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: US midterms: Democrats projected to win Congress in major setback for Trump
items.description: Democrats have won full control of the US Congress in a sweeping midterm rout on Tuesday, with a series of upsets delivering a major rebuke to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party, according to media projections. The victory handed Democrats both the House of Representatives and Senate, giving them power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times : “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats”. But minutes later on social media the 80-year-old signalled how he intends to deal with Democratic attempts to pass laws, posting a picture of a red baseball cap emblazoned: “VETO.” The Democrats’ decisive Senate breakthroughs came in Kansas and Iowa, the fifth and sixth Republican-held seats to fall in the extraordinary “blue wave” election night. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008, again illustrating the scale of party’s inroads into Republican strongholds. Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton speaks following her victory in the US midterm elections at a Democratic Election Night rally, in Columbus, Ohio, US, November 3, 2026. — Reuters The upsets followed victories in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, where voters rejected Republican candidates despite Trump’s intensive efforts to rally his supporters. Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office. Talarico that “we defeated Goliath” after winning a US Senate seat over Texas attorney General Ken Paxton, a close ally of President Donald Trump who was heavily backed by tech billionaire Elon Musk. “In this race, we went up against our own Goliaths. The richest man in the world, the most powerful man in the world, and the entire Washington, DC establishment,” Talarico told a victory rally in the Texas capital, Austin. Democrats also protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. Republicans had held a 53-47 Senate majority. The six-seat Democratic gain proved sufficient for networks to project a takeover despite some races remaining unresolved. Republican heartland Democrats also captured the House after flipping Republican-held districts in states stretching from Pennsylvania and New Jersey to Kentucky, Arizona and North Carolina. Some victories came in territory Trump had carried comfortably in 2024, despite Republican attempts to shore up House seats by redrawing electoral boundaries. One bellwether was Indiana, where Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump won by 17 points. Analysts had identified an upset there as a warning of a much wider Democratic advance. Supporters react to early election results in favor of US Senator Jon Ossoff at an election night watch party hosted by the Democratic Party of Georgia after the midterms election in Atlanta, Georgia on November 3, 2026. — AFP In Georgia, former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor in US history, while other Democratic gains extended to statehouses across the country. Republicans had some bright spots in Florida, where Trump-backed Byron Donalds won the governorship, becoming the state’s first Black governor, and Ashley Moody kept a Senate seat. George Washington University professor Todd Belt called the Democratic advance “a big wipeout and a strong repudiation of Donald Trump and his policies,” citing voters’ concerns about the economy, corruption and the Iran conflict. Trump on defensive Democrats will now be able to block Trump’s legislation, investigate his administration over corruption allegations, the Iran war and immigration enforcement, and use Senate control to thwart judicial appointments and senior nominations. Robert Garcia, a Democrat expected to lead the powerful House Oversight Committee, warned Republicans on social media: “LAWYER UP.” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries declared Trump’s MAGA movement “on the run from sea to shining sea.” House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) speaks during a press conference with the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) at the AC Hotel Washington DC Capitol Hill Navy Yard on November 03, 2026 in Washington, DC. Jeffries is also positioned to become the first Black speaker of the House when the new Congress convenes in January, if elected by his colleagues. For many voters, the central concern was Trump’s stewardship of the economy. “Rent, groceries, utility bills, and property taxes keep climbing,” 24-year-old Los Angeles voter Taylor Cook told AFP. A rebuke to Trump, winner says “In sweeping and decisive victories, the American people have rebuked the depravity, corruption and incompetence of the man named President Donald J. Trump,” incumbent Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff, the projected winner in Georgia, told supporters at a victory party. In Florida, Republican Senator Ashley Moody fended off Democrat Angie Nixon but was ahead by only about three percentage points in a state Trump carried by 13 points in 2024, according to a vote count compiled by Reuters and USA Today , further evidence that even solidly Republican states were shifting dramatically toward Democrats. Democrats held onto three House districts in Florida that Republican lawmakers had redrawn earlier this year, all of which backed Trump by at least nine percentage points, according to media projections. Cait Conley, Democratic candidate for the US House of Representatives in New York’s 17th Congressional District, reacts following her victory in the US midterm elections, in Pleasantville, New York, US, November 3, 2026. — Reuters Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, a former mayor of Atlanta, on Tuesday was elected governor of the state of Georgia, becoming the first Black woman elected to that office in the US, media projections showed. CNN and NBC News called the race in her favour. Bottoms defeated billionaire health care executive Rick Jackson, who ran as a Republican. Current Governor Brian Kemp is term-limited and could not run again. Midterm elections are typically viewed as a referendum on the president, and that is especially true for Trump, who dominates attention like no other politician. Trump himself told his supporters to “pretend I’m on the ballot” and held dozens of rallies in the closing weeks. According to exit polls conducted by SSRS on behalf of a consortium of US media outlets, including major television networks and the Associated Press , half of voters nationwide said they saw the 2026 midterm elections as an opportunity to rebuke the president, and three-quarters said they are “angry” or “dissatisfied” with the way the country is headed. In addition, 70 per cent of voters surveyed said they want Congress to provide more checks and balances on the president. History is against Republicans: the sitting president’s party has lost ground in Congress in all but two midterms since World War Two. Trump’s approval rating is hovering near his career lows, with voters frustrated by war on Iran , higher fuel prices and wider affordability concerns. Led by Trump, Republicans have portrayed Democratic candidates as radical, un-American and even communist, labels Democrats flatly reject. Opinion polls show voters are most concerned about affordability and disapprove of Trump’s handling of the issue. His tariffs on imports, many of which the courts threw out, and his decision to attack Iran in February raised prices for consumers. Trump deploys election monitors The US Justice Department said it had deployed 1,000 election monitors and observers to all 50 states in what it called the largest Election Day monitoring effort in history. Democrats criticised the plan as potential voter intimidation. In roughly two-thirds of the jurisdictions the department listed, voters supported Democrat Kamala Harris over Trump in the 2024 presidential election, a Reuters analysis found. Election officials in several states reported no issues with the monitoring effort. New Mexico’s secretary of state’s office said it had received reports of federal monitors asking “unusual questions” in one county and that the Justice Department offered assurances that the conduct would be addressed.

items.title: APC group questions Imo council poll suspension, warns against anti-party activities
items.description: The APC South East Integrity Movement has called on Governor Hope Uzodimma to explain the indefinite postponement of local government elections in Imo State, particularly after arrangements for the exercise had reportedly been completed. The group also warned that the All Progressives Congress (APC) would not tolerate any form of anti-party activity by its members ahead of the 2027 general elections. The APC group, in a statement issued in Enugu on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and signed by Chijioke Afamefuna, expressed concern that the council elections were postponed after preparations had been concluded, raising questions about the reasons behind the decision. It questioned why the state government would suspend the exercise at that stage without providing what it considered a satisfactory explanation, and called on the governor to clarify the circumstances surrounding the postponement. The group urged the APC national leadership to investigate the development and ensure that the party’s interests were protected in the state. It said the party would not condone actions by any of its members that could undermine its electoral prospects or strengthen the position of opposition parties, adding that members should remain committed to the party’s decisions and objectives. The movement also expressed concern about the implications of the postponement for the APC’s political structures in Imo, particularly its preparations for the 2027 elections. Citing the Supreme Court’s July 2024 judgment on local government autonomy, the group appealed to the Federal Government, the Central Bank of Nigeria, the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission to ensure that local government funds were administered in line with the court’s position on elected council administrations. It argued that local government allocations should not be channelled through caretaker arrangements and urged the relevant authorities to ensure that elected council officials were in place. The group also referred to the dispute over local government administration in Osun State, where the handling of statutory allocations became a subject of controversy following the February 2025 council elections and subsequent legal proceedings. It urged the APC to uphold its position on local government autonomy and apply the same principles consistently across states, irrespective of the political party in control. items.title: Ressortissants burkinabè à Siguiri : Ouagadougou parle d’expulsion et organise leur retour
items.description: Le gouvernement burkinabè annonce des mesures pour accompagner le retour de plusieurs milliers de ses ressortissants qui vivaient à Siguiri, en Haute-Guinée, où ils exerçaient des activités sur des sites d’exploitation artisanale de l’or. Selon l’Agence d’information du Burkina (AIB), dans une dépêche publiée mardi 3 novembre 2026, les autorités burkinabè ont pris des dispositions pour assurer le retour de leurs compatriotes « dans la dignité et la décence ». Dans ce cadre, une délégation gouvernementale du Burkina Faso est annoncée au Mali ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026. Elle aura pour mission d’apporter l’assistance nécessaire aux ressortissants burkinabè concernés, présentés comme étant en situation de détresse. Les autorités de Ouagadougou appellent par ailleurs les populations au calme et à la retenue. Elles les exhortent à ne pas céder à la manipulation et à la désinformation autour de cette situation. Cette annonce intervient dans un contexte marqué par les opérations de nettoyage et de contrôle engagées par les autorités guinéennes dans la préfecture de Siguiri. Celles-ci ont notamment décrété l’interdiction totale de l’exploitation artisanale de l’or dans cette zone, confrontée à une dégradation préoccupante de son environnement sous l’effet de pratiques minières préjudiciables à l’écosystème. Les autorités guinéennes insistent toutefois sur le fait que ces opérations ne visent aucune communauté étrangère en particulier. Elles précisent que les mesures engagées concernent l’ensemble des exploitants exerçant illégalement dans le secteur de l’exploitation artisanale de l’or, sans distinction de nationalité. L’objectif affiché est de faire respecter la réglementation minière, de lutter contre les pratiques clandestines et de préserver l’environnement. Dans le cadre de cette opération, le chef de l’État guinéen, Mamadi Doumbouya, a également procédé au limogeage de plusieurs hauts responsables dans le contexte du dossier de l’exploitation aurifère illégale à Siguiri. De son côté, la ministre de l’Administration du territoire et de la Décentralisation, Djénabou Touré, a annoncé, le 3 novembre, le limogeage de 479 présidents de districts et de quartiers dans la région administrative de Siguiri. Ces différentes mesures s’inscrivent dans la volonté affichée des autorités guinéennes de reprendre le contrôle de l’exploitation artisanale de l’or et de mettre fin aux pratiques irrégulières qui affectent cette importante zone aurifère du pays. Ousmane CAMARA L’article Ressortissants burkinabè à Siguiri : Ouagadougou parle d’expulsion et organise leur retour est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Sanusi credits Tinubu for rescuing Nigeria’s economy from brink
items.description: The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, has said President Bola Tinubu deserves credit for bringing Nigeria’s economy back from the brink, citing improvements in economic growth, inflation, foreign reserves and export diversification. Sanusi, however, cautioned that significant economic challenges remain, saying the country must sustain its current growth trajectory to achieve lasting stability. The former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) spoke on Tuesday at the Oxford Global Think Tank conference convened by Arunma Oteh. “I’m not a fan of politicians, but we need to give credit to President Tinubu’s administration for bringing us back from the brink,” he said. Sanusi cited the country’s economic growth of 4.48 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, describing it as an improvement over the average performance recorded during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari. “GDP in Q2 2026 was at 4.48 percent. It’s not as high as it was under the Yar’Adua/Jonathan government, but during the Buhari years, the economy grew by 0.9 percent. Today it’s at 4.5 percent. That’s progress,” he said. He also highlighted the decline in inflation from about 30 per cent to 14.6 per cent, noting that it was projected to fall further to 12.5 per cent by the end of the year. On economic growth and living standards, the emir said Nigeria’s gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, measured in dollar terms, had increased by 47 per cent since 2023. He expressed optimism that sustaining the current pace of growth could restore the country’s GDP per capita to its 2005 level by the end of next year. “If we continue at this rate, by the end of next year, GDP per capita will be back to where it was in 2005,” he said. Sanusi also pointed to Nigeria’s foreign reserves, which he put at $55 billion, but warned that a substantial portion of the inflows was driven by foreign portfolio investments, which could be volatile. “Our reserves are at $55 billion, and yes, a lot of it is driven by portfolio flows, which are volatile,” he said. He attributed the continued inflows partly to high oil prices amid the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz and attractive returns available to investors in Nigeria. On export diversification, Sanusi said 20 per cent of Nigeria’s exports were coming from the Dangote Refinery, describing the development as evidence of progress beyond the country’s traditional export sources. Despite acknowledging the economic gains, the former CBN governor criticised the Tinubu administration’s communication strategy, saying the government appeared to interpret criticism and constructive suggestions as attacks. “This government doesn’t express itself properly. It sees every suggestion and contribution it does not like as an attack, and it doesn’t have good spokespersons,” he said. Sanusi nevertheless maintained that the administration had begun laying the foundations for economic stability, stressing that the progress recorded so far should be regarded as a starting point rather than an end in itself. “There are clearly foundations being laid for stability. It’s not the end, but the first step towards stability,” he said. The post Sanusi credits Tinubu for rescuing Nigeria’s economy from brink appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nasa's Swift satellite telescope heads for fiery re-entry 22 years after launch
items.description: An aging Nasa satellite telescope that a robotic spacecraft was sent to retrieve on a failed rescue mission this summer was headed for a fiery re-entry into Earth’s atmosphere on Wednesday, nearly 22 years after it was launched into orbit. The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory , weighing roughly 3,200 pounds (1,452 kg), was set to tumble out of orbit and burn up in the atmosphere somewhere over the tropics, with fragments surviving re-entry unlikely to threaten populated areas, according to Nasa. The US Space Force has put the odds of harm coming to anyone on Earth at one chance in 2,100, Nasa said in an online statement, projecting the time of re-entry at approximately 3:30am EST (0830 GMT). The Aerospace Corporation, a nonprofit national security research entity, projected a re-entry window of 5:19am EST, plus or minus two hours. London-based astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell, an honorary professor at the Durham University Space Research Centre, cited revised US Space Force data predicting re-entry most likely to come around 7:45am EST. “The satellite is in a very circular orbit, skimming the top of the atmosphere,” he told Reuters by phone on Tuesday night. “The question is at what point does it heat up enough that it starts breaking up.” Nasa’s prized $500 million Swift satellite, a first-of-its-kind multi-wavelength space observatory, has been studying gamma-ray bursts and other cosmic phenomena since 2004, using its array of three telescopes. The observatory, which has no onboard propulsion system of its own, has been drifting toward an expected demise for months as it circles the globe at a speed of roughly 17,000 miles per hour (27,359 kph). Astronomers had hoped to extend Swift’s mission for a number of years by giving the satellite telescope a lift. In July, Nasa and Arizona-based startup Katalyst launched a specially built rescue vehicle called LINK on a mission to rendezvous with Swift, latch onto the satellite and tug the observatory back into a higher, more sustainable orbit. But the LINK spacecraft itself began spinning uncontrollably soon after reaching space, and by mid-August, mission managers abandoned the effort, resigned to letting Swift continue to meet its fate. The aborted rescue attempt, the first US mission of its kind, took on heightened significance as a demonstration of a new orbital grappling technology seen as pivotal to the outcome of the US-China space race. The LINK effort was closely watched as a trial run of a key satellite-maintenance technology with potential dual-use military space applications. Katalyst touted the mission as a historic endeavor that designed, built and tested the LINK rescue vehicle on an unprecedented nine-month production schedule under a $30 million Nasa contract. Swift was launched more than two decades ago to explore the most powerful known explosions in the universe, bursts of gamma-ray radiation emanating from the cores of distant galaxies. Originally designed for a two-year prime mission, Swift remained in operation far longer with observations of a wide range of cosmic objects, from galaxies powered by supermassive black holes and stars emitting X-ray flares, to comets and asteroids streaking through our own solar system.

items.title: Football world mourns Tenerife striker De Miguel
items.description: The world of football has come together to mourn the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel . The forward suffered head and chest injuries in a heavy collision with goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Spanish second division match against FC Andorra on Monday. De Miguel’s condition was described as stable but serious on Monday, but his health deteriorated on Tuesday morning and the Spaniard died at 07:00 GMT. A minute’s silence was held before Tuesday evening’s Champions League matches across Europe. That will be repeated for Wednesday’s fixtures, as well as all Europa League and Conference League matches this week. Mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez, Tenerife’s home ground. Tenerife said in a statement on Tuesday evening they will commence six official days of mourning, with all club activities suspended during this time. The club’s players, staff and officials will attend De Miguel’s funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, Toledo. Tenerife will also open their home ground on Saturday evening to allow supporters to “bid a fitting farewell”. “Jesus de Miguel’s family would like to thank everyone for their messages of support and, from the bottom of their hearts, ask that their privacy be respected at this terrible time. May he rest in peace,” added the statement. Jesus de Miguel joined Tenerife in 2025 on a three-year deal “We are torn by the news,” said Fran Leon, president of Tenerife’s federation of supporters’ clubs. “All of the island is in mourning. All of Canarias is in mourning. It’s a shared pain.” Fan David Tejera said De Miguel’s “effort” and “passion” for Tenerife would endure. “You are already part of the blue and white history,” he said. Tenerife and Andorra were tied 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred. Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel. The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife’s ground to hospital. Players from both teams were visibly distressed by the incident, with a number of De Miguel’s team-mates in tears. Before Spanish club Villareal’s fixture against Paris St-Germain, fans held up a sign that read ‘DEP’ – which translates to descanse en paz, or rest in peace in English ‘Very difficult moment’ for Owono Reuters reported on Tuesday that police in Spain have opened an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel’s death. Under Spanish law, any death that is deemed non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry. Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui told Spanish news agency EFE that criminal proceedings were “very unlikely”. The referee showed Owono a straight red card before abandoning the match. The goalkeeper, who had over 30,000 followers on Instagram on Tuesday morning, has since deactivated his account. Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho expressed his sadness over the incident and said it is a “very, very difficult moment” for Owono. “I think it’s something very shocking for the world in general, so imagine for the world of football, for people like us who are on the pitch competing every day,” he said. “It’s hard, it’s sad. Obviously, all our words and feelings go out to the family and friends of the player who passed away, and I also think this has to be a very, very, very difficult moment for the other player [Owono] involved in the situation. “It’s sad for everyone.” After scoring twice in Barcelona’s win over Aston Villa, Brazilian forward Raphinha said: “Today I don’t want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus – may he rest in peace. “From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family.”

items.title: Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis
items.description: By Udeme Akpan Power sector experts have called for accelerated deployment of renewable energy and microgrids to address Nigeria’s persistent electricity supply challenges and reduce dependence on the national grid. Speaking in separate interviews with Vanguard at the recently concluded Nigeria Energy Summit in Lagos, they said decentralised power solutions would improve electricity access, particularly for businesses and rural communities. Product Manager, DEIF, Anshul Alankar, said: “The reality is that renewable energy is the in-thing, and government policy also supports it. It is important to latch on to it as early as possible, especially for the commercial sector and even for individual users. “The grid system is not able to provide all the electricity and power needed by Nigerians and Africans to maintain sustainable energy. “Nigeria has surplus solar energy, and microgrids will help because you don’t need huge infrastructure to bring power across the country. “Microgrids are a more efficient way of handling local and rural areas. You can create your own grid, minimise fuel consumption and maximise the sun, which is free.” On the growing demand for decentralised energy, he said: “We see that the need of the market is around microgrids and fuel efficiency. We provide solutions that enable batteries to work more efficiently and solar panels to be maximised.” Also speaking, Executive Director, Delmira Power Solutions, Dr. Moriam Jagun, said the company was bringing advanced power management solutions into Nigeria. She said its technologies “coordinate, protect and monitor energy, making sure that energy is efficiently generated and delivered, both for land and marine.” Sales Head, Engineering, Delmira Power Solutions, Engr. Nmecha Chizinum Ayodele, said: “Our country has come to the point of further expansion in renewable energy, from household to grid levels.” He added: “DEIF solutions can remotely monitor, automate and synchronise different power sources to provide all-round power for industries and homes, thereby reducing the cost of energy.” The post Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigeria’s high production costs threaten industrial competitiveness — Feese
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Nigeria Economic Summit Group has warned that high production costs, unreliable electricity and poor logistics infrastructure are undermining Nigeria’s industrial competitiveness, calling for a council within the Presidency to coordinate industrialisation policies. Co-facilitator of the NESG, Lumun Feese, said Nigeria needed a coordinated approach to industrial development to address structural challenges and enable local manufacturers to compete effectively in African markets. She spoke at a breakout session on building an integrated industrial ecosystem during the 32nd Nigeria Economic Summit on Tuesday in Abuja. Feese said Nigeria had dropped from eighth to 14th position on the African Development Bank’s Africa Industrialisation Index, although she noted that the methodology had changed and more countries had been included in the latest ranking. She said, “We are not maximising our potential and our large economy. “How do we go and compete in South Africa when our cost of production is so high? Power, logistics and so on and so forth.” She added that Nigeria needed to move beyond its domestic market and develop the capacity to supply other African countries. Feese said the proposed industrialisation, competitiveness and regional integration council would provide a central coordinating platform within the Presidency to align government policies, improve implementation of the National Industrial Policy and strengthen private-sector participation. She said Nigerian businesses needed reliable power, efficient transportation systems and lower production costs to take advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area, which offers access to a wider continental market. Feese said the recommendations followed consultations on mining, the blue economy, power, oil and gas, and industrial competitiveness. She urged businesses and other stakeholders to sustain their engagement with the NESG’s Industrial Policy Commission, saying coordinated policies and consistent implementation were necessary to achieve measurable industrial growth. items.title: ADC vows to proceed with Sokoto campaign despite intimidation
items.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has vowed to proceed with its scheduled campaign in Sokoto State despite what it described as attempts by the state government to intimidate the opposition and obstruct its political activities. The party also warned that Governor Ahmed Aliyu would be held responsible if any violence was directed at opposition members or supporters in the state. The ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, stated this in a statement issued on Tuesday, accusing the Sokoto State Government of undermining democratic rights and deliberately frustrating the party’s activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Abdullahi said the party would not be deterred by the alleged intimidation, insisting that no governor had the authority to prevent any political party from campaigning or presenting its candidates to voters. “The Sokoto State Government must understand that governing a state does not confer ownership. Public office is a temporary mandate from the people, not a licence to suppress political competition,” the statement read. “No governor has the power to decide which party can campaign, which candidate can speak, or which political choices the people of Sokoto are allowed to consider.” The ADC spokesperson called on the state government to immediately stop what he described as efforts to frustrate its lawful political activities and guarantee a level playing field for all political parties. He also reminded security agencies and other public institutions that their responsibility was to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, rather than the political interests of the ruling party. Abdullahi warned that public officials who abused their authority to obstruct lawful political activities would face the legal consequences of their actions. “Let there be no misunderstanding. The ADC will campaign in Sokoto State. We will not be intimidated, obstructed or pushed out of any part of Nigeria simply because those in power are afraid of political competition,” he said. He maintained that democratic participation was a constitutional right and not a privilege to be granted by elected public officials. The ADC spokesperson further accused the ruling party of displaying intolerance towards opposition activities, challenging it to submit itself to an open contest if it believed it had performed well in government. READ ALSO: ADC accuses Sokoto govt of intimidation, demands reopening of campaign office “If the ruling party believes it has served the people well, it should have nothing to fear from an open contest,” he said. “Intimidation cannot manufacture public support, and obstruction cannot take away the people’s right to choose their leaders. The people of Sokoto, like all Nigerians, deserve the opportunity to listen to competing ideas and make their own decisions.” He urged party members, supporters and residents of Sokoto State to remain peaceful and law-abiding, while assuring that the ADC would continue to defend its right to campaign freely across the country. “The future of Sokoto belongs to the people of Sokoto, not to any governor or political party. No government has the right to veto democracy,” Abdullahi added. The development follows the sealing of the ADC’s campaign office in Sokoto over an alleged ownership dispute. The state’s Commissioner for Lands and Housing, Nasiru Dantsoho, had announced the sealing of the building on Monday, saying the action followed a recent clash involving supporters of different political parties. The ADC had earlier accused the state government of using the police to intimidate opposition politicians and demanded the immediate reopening of the premises. items.title: Champions League: Inter win comfortably in Feyenoord
items.description: Inter Milan bounced back from their derby defeat with a comfortable Champions League victory over Feyenoord. Inter’s unbeaten start to the Serie A season came to an end at the San Siro on Saturday as they fell to a 3-1 defeat by neighbours AC Milan. But, after claiming just three points in their opening three Champions League matches, the Italian champions got back on track with an assured victory at Stadion Feijenoord. Played in by Spence, Yann Bisseck put the visitors in front inside eight minutes with a sublime curling finish from the edge of the box. Pio Esposito doubled the lead in the 34th minute when he pounced on Spence’s deflected strike and headed home from close range. Poland midfielder Piotr Zielinski added the third after darting across Feyenoord’s box and bending a brilliant strike beyond Tjark Ernst. Esposito thought he had scored his second of the evening when he tapped in from six yards, but it was quickly ruled out for offside. Spence, who played a starring role in England’s run to the World Cup semi-finals, left Tottenham for Inter in August and his side are 14th in the league phase table on six points. By sitting 30th in the standings on three points after four games, Feyenoord face a battle to qualify for the play-offs. The Dutch side welcome Porto in their next Champions League outing on Tuesday, 24 November, while Inter host Stuttgart the following day.

items.title: Petrol hits N1,370/litre as depot prices rise
items.description: By Udeme Akpan The pump price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), popularly known as petrol, has risen to N1,370 per litre in Lagos, following fresh increases in depot prices across major supply locations. Checks by Vanguard on Tuesday showed that MRS and NNPC filling stations sold petrol at N1,360 per litre, while Mobil sold at N1,349. Some independent marketers sold at between N1,365 and N1,370, depending on location. The increase followed sharp movements in depot prices, particularly in Lagos, where A.A. Rano raised its PMS price by N75 to N1,295 per litre, while African Terminal, Aiteo and Integrated increased their prices to about N1,300. NIPCO also raised its price by N55 to N1,305, while Dangote’s price edged up by N3 to N1,303. MRS retained its depot price at N1,310. In Port Harcourt, Matrix increased its PMS price by N15 to N1,300 per litre, while Bulk Strategic, Masters and T.S.L remained at N1,300. Warri also recorded increases, with A.Y.M. Shafa and Matrix raising their prices by N17 each to N1,300, while Parker moved up by N15 to the same level. Calabar recorded higher PMS prices, with Fynefield and Northwest at N1,360 per litre. Meanwhile, Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), or diesel, recorded mixed movements. In Lagos, WOSBAB cut its AGO price by N21 to N1,809 per litre, while Bulk Strategic reduced its price by N15 to N1,835. Rain Oil and Dangote also reduced their prices to N1,850 and N1,823 respectively. In Warri, Matrix and Rain Oil cut their AGO prices by N5 each to N1,835 per litre, while Edo Refinery, NIPCO and Prudent retained theirs at N1,840. The latest figures point to continued volatility in the downstream market as changes in depot prices filter through to retail outlets. “To safeguard port integrity and vessel safety, all maritime operators, terminal users, and personnel must utilise authorised reporting protocols immediately upon detecting any security incident or anomaly,” the agency stated. items.title: NIMASA threatens sanctions over missing marine incident reports
items.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) has threatened sanctions against Port Facility Security Officers (PFSOs) who fail to properly report marine security incidents, warning that bypassing approved reporting channels constitutes a breach of international port security rules. The warning followed concerns that incident reports from port facilities were being sent to individual NIMASA officials instead of the agency’s designated International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Unit. In a notice signed by Mudi Isa, Head, ISPS Code Unit, the agency directed all PFSOs to route incident reports through the approved ISPS Unit email address. The notice, titled “Non-Receipt of Incident Reports/Submission to Approved ISPS Unit,” said: “It has come to our attention that the Unit is currently not receiving your incident report emails, which poses a significant risk.” NIMASA warned that the failure to use the prescribed channel could have serious implications for maritime security. “Failure to report security incidents to the correct channels constitutes a breach of ISPS compliance,” it stated. The agency specifically directed port facility security personnel to stop sending or copying reports to individual NIMASA staff emails unless expressly authorised. “Do not copy or send reports to individual staff emails unless explicitly authorised,” the notice stated. NIMASA also directed PFSOs to confirm receipt of every incident report and contact the ISPS Unit immediately if no acknowledgement was received within 24 hours. “If you do not receive an acknowledgment from the ISPS Unit within 24hrs of submission, contact the Unit immediately via phone,” it said. The agency further advised operators who were unsure of the approved reporting directory to contact the ISPS Unit for verification before submitting their reports. NIMASA said the directive was aimed at ensuring that security incidents and anomalies are captured promptly and handled through a coordinated response mechanism. items.title: Nigeria’s exports record 25% increase in 2yrs — NPA
items.description: By Godwin Oritse Nigeria’s exports have increased by 25 per cent in the last two years, driven by Federal Government reforms and improved collaboration with port terminal operators, the Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, has said. Speaking at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference in London, organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH), Dantsoho said the growth covered both oil and non-oil exports. “For us in Nigeria, the most important thing is that we are seeing growth as a result of this policy that we are taking. Statistically, the exports from Nigeria in the last two years has increased by 25 per cent. “These are exports that are not mainly only oil and gas. In manufacturing and agriculture, raw materials like cocoa and cashew, volumes have increased, and that is to the credit of the partnership between ourselves and the major terminal operators, APM Terminals,” he said. He attributed the improvement to Export Processing Terminals established by the NPA. “We have got about four of those in Nigeria where we collaborate with the terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other agencies that have a stake, so that everything regarding the processing of cargo for export is done locally,” he stated. On the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), Dantsoho said: “Nigeria’s economy is very strong now because of our president’s reforms, which everyone can testify is attracting investors to the country.” He added that port reforms had improved operational efficiency and increased revenue. “We have experienced a lot of increase in volumes and revenue that has been generated by the ports across Nigeria. As a matter of fact, the efficiency in the ports in Nigeria is far better now than those of other West African countries,” he said. Dantsoho also disclosed that the Federal Government was investing $1 billion in expanding and modernising Apapa Port, with private-sector partnerships supporting infrastructure and technology development. items.title: US Midterms: Trump accepts midterm results, pledges to work with Democrats
items.description: United States President Donald Trump has said he is prepared to accept the outcome of the country’s midterm elections and work with Democrats, as results showed the opposition party heading towards control of both chambers of Congress. Trump made the remarks on Tuesday night during a telephone interview with The New York Times, as he monitored election results at the White House. “We’ll, you know, look forward to working with them,” he said. “We’ll probably work something out.” The President’s comments came amid major Republican losses, with Democrats making significant gains in closely contested races and threatening Republican control of Congress. Trump attributed his party’s poor performance partly to his absence from the ballot, suggesting that his participation could have changed the outcome. He also defended his decision to launch a war against Iran, describing it as a “very wise decision”. The President further said he had no regrets about endorsing Republican candidates, including South Carolina Senator Darline Graham and Texas Attorney-General Ken Paxton, who both lost their Senate bids. Speaking shortly before 10:30pm on Tuesday, Trump said he was following the election results during the interview. “I’m just looking at these results as I’m talking,” he said. Reacting to Graham’s defeat, he added: “I see that Darline lost. Wow, that’s amazing. How do you think Lindsey would have done if he ran?” He was referring to Senator Lindsey Graham, who reportedly died in July. Democrats were on course to take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate as results continued to emerge, PUNCH Online had reported on Wednesday. A Democratic takeover of Congress would significantly alter the balance of political power in Washington, potentially subjecting Trump’s administration to increased congressional scrutiny and making it more difficult for the President to advance his legislative agenda during the remaining two years of his term. items.title: ADC accuses Sokoto govt of intimidation, demands reopening of campaign office
items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Sokoto State Government of using the police to intimidate opposition politicians and frustrate its political activities, following the sealing of its state campaign office in Sokoto. The party demanded the immediate reopening of the premises, describing the action as illegal and an infringement on its constitutional rights ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the ADC said its campaign office along Ahmadu Bello Way in Sokoto metropolis was sealed on Tuesday, November 3, by officers of the Sokoto State Police Command allegedly acting on the orders of the state government. The development occurred barely hours before the commencement of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in the state, with the proposed campaign venue reportedly remaining locked. The statement was signed by Yusuf Suleiman, also known as Dan Amar Sokoto, Deputy Director-General of Administration of the Atiku Abubakar ADC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, and made available to journalists. The party alleged that the premises were sealed without a court order, prior notice or any lawful explanation from the authorities. It described the action as “illegal, unconstitutional and reckless”, arguing that it violated its rights to freedom of association, peaceful assembly and political participation. The ADC also cited Section 95 of the Electoral Act 2026, arguing that the action undermined the legal protections available to registered political parties to organise and conduct their activities without unlawful interference. The party further linked the development to what it described as a pattern of political intimidation in the state, recalling an alleged attack on its governorship candidate, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, at Sultan Sadiq Abubakar International Airport four days earlier. It dismissed suggestions that the authorities might not have known who occupied the building, insisting that the party had operated openly from the premises for more than eight years. “The claim that the authorities do not know who occupies the building is not credible. The ADC has operated openly from those premises for more than eight years,” the statement said. The party argued that any genuine inquiry into the ownership or occupation of the property should have been made through a formal letter rather than the deployment of armed police officers to seal its premises. It also alleged that the state government was concerned about the growing support for the ADC and its candidates, accusing it of responding to political competition with force rather than democratic engagement. “We reject this conduct in its entirety. We will pursue every legitimate and lawful remedy available to us to reopen our office and to protect our members, our supporters and our property in Sokoto,” it stated. The ADC held the state government and the police command responsible for any breach of peace that might arise from the closure. It consequently called on the Inspector-General of Police to direct the immediate reopening of the premises and ensure that the police discharged their responsibilities impartially towards all political parties. The party also appealed to civil society organisations, election observers and the international community to condemn the action and demand explanations from the Sokoto State Government and the police. It specifically urged Nigeria’s international partners, including the United States, United Kingdom, European Union, France, Germany, Italy and the Commonwealth, to take note of what it described as actions undermining democratic governance in the state and consider visa restrictions against individuals found responsible for subverting democratic processes. “Democracy in Sokoto will not be locked away. The people of Sokoto will be heard,” the party declared. Vanguard Newspaper The post ADC accuses Sokoto govt of intimidation, demands reopening of campaign office appeared first on Vanguard News .

The award recognises the refrigerator’s distinctive design and smart features, including customisable LED door panels and smart connectivity, which allow users to personalise their kitchen experience. Beyond its aesthetics, LG’s refrigerator range addresses practical household needs such as food preservation, energy efficiency and durability, which remain important considerations for Nigerian consumers. The company offers top-freezer, bottom-freezer, side-by-side and premium refrigerator models designed to accommodate different household sizes and lifestyles. One of its products, the GN-F452PFAQ Top Freezer Refrigerator, features FRESH Converter+ technology, which allows users to adjust temperature settings to suit different food types and maintain optimal freshness. It also comes with an automatic ice maker for added convenience. Selected LG refrigerator models are equipped with Smart Inverter Compressor , LINEARCooling and DoorCooling+ technologies, designed to improve energy efficiency, provide consistent cooling and preserve food freshness for longer. These features are particularly relevant to households seeking reliable refrigeration, lower energy consumption and dependable appliance performance. The recognition at the BRANDCOM Awards further highlights LG’s presence in Nigeria’s competitive refrigerator market. items.title: Democrats take control of US Congress as voters reject Trump’s Republicans
items.description: President Donald Trump told voters to pretend he was on the ballot in this year’s midterm elections. They did. And they resoundingly rejected both his policies and his Republican Party. Democrats have captured full control of Congress, NBC News projects, with voters delivering a forceful repudiation of Trump’s agenda, coupled with a clear-cut message that Congress has not done enough to provide checks on his administration and needs to do more to address affordability and corruption. Democrats’ victory in the Senate comes after a swift and decisive win in the House, where Democrats are set to have what could be their largest majority in nearly two decades. Democrats flipped five Republican-held seats in Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas — a state they’ve long dreamed of turning blue. In a number of those states, Trump handpicked the nominees, sometimes over the objections of members of his own party who were concerned that they would be weak in the general election. An early warning sign that it would be a tough night for Republicans came when South Carolina — a state even many Democrats thought was out of reach — fell early. Democrats made incursions deep into the heart of MAGA country, with gains far beyond what they were able to achieve in the 2018 midterm elections during Trump’s first term. Forty-three percent of midterm voters surveyed in the NBC News Exit Poll said one of the reasons they voted the way they did was to express opposition to Trump, whose job approval rating is lower than that of any president on Election Day in nearly two decades. Seventy-one percent of voters — including 41% of Republicans — also said there is not enough congressional oversight of Trump. Corruption, affordability, immigration and the war in Iran were all key issues, as well. The results were so bleak that Trump quickly ran away from them Tuesday evening. Trump said on social media that, in fact, he was not on the ballot , and that’s why Republicans lost: “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” The Democratic takeover will reverberate widely. With majorities in both chambers, the Trump administration will now have to contend with checks and investigations it avoided with a compliant Congress in Republican hands. The election results could influence the makeup of the Supreme Court, the arc of the 2028 presidential race and the fate of Trump’s legislative plans in the back half of his term. But it also sets up an epic showdown with Trump that will test the constitutional power-sharing arrangement that has weathered war and civil strife over the past two centuries — but survived intact. With their newly minted majority, Democratic lawmakers will acquire an arsenal of oversight powers they’ll use to investigate a Trump administration they contend has escaped accountability. Trump, in turn, has built a presidency rooted in a vision of unrivaled executive power. Neither side seems in a mood to compromise, meaning the next two years could bring legislative and executive branch clashes unlike anything since the Watergate era. “What we’re going to do is lower costs, end all this rampant corruption and end the chaos. Plain and simple,” Chuck Schumer of New York, the Senate’s Democratic leader, said before the election in response to a question from NBC News about his priorities if his party won. Democrats’ sweeping victory looked inconceivable when the midterm campaign season kicked off. The party prevailed despite an unfavorable map in which the major battlegrounds ran through red states that Trump won in all three of his presidential bids. Not since 2006 has the minority party flipped control of both chambers on a single night. Then-President George W. Bush, facing a voter backlash over the Iraq War, memorably lamented that the outcome was “a thumping.” Trump sought to mobilize his core voters and preserve the GOP’s narrow majority in the House and the Senate by putting himself front and center. He kept up a packed campaign schedule in the final month of the campaign, but he and his party were dogged by his low job approval ratings , along with pronounced voter frustration with the economy. Trump sought to blame his predecessor, Joe Biden, for rising prices, but voters didn’t seem to buy the argument. Gas prices spiked after Trump and Israeli leaders launched the Iran war in late February, and Americans disliked Trump’s handling of the conflict, creating another drag on Republican candidacies. The election results are apt to make history, with House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., on the cusp of becoming the country’s first Black House speaker. Democrats are expected to hold their internal leadership elections the week of Nov. 16, when Jeffries will become his party’s nominee for speaker. Then, on Jan. 3, he must win 218 votes — a simple majority of all House members — to formally win the speaker’s gavel and become second in the line of presidential succession. Schumer, who previously served four years as Senate majority leader, is expected to return to the top job once again after he exceeded expectations and led his party back from exile. Democrats had been favored to win the House all season; they needed to flip a net of just three GOP-held seats to do so, and historically, the president’s party loses dozens of seats on average during midterm elections. But as the campaign unfolded, Democrats grew more bullish about winning the Senate, as well. One reason was the minority vote. Latino voters helped propel Trump’s political comeback in 2024, but they turned away from him this cycle, citing high prices and his immigration crackdown. An NBC News poll released Sunday showed that Democrats enjoyed a 27-point lead among Latino voters, a marked contrast from the election in 2024, when Trump lost by only 7 points in the demographic. The outcome could also leave an imprint on the Supreme Court. Before the election, multiple Senate Democrats cast doubt on whether they would confirm any Trump nominee to a vacancy on the Supreme Court if one were to arise in his final two years. With full control of the Senate, Democrats are positioned to block nominees Trump puts forward. “Well, given the history of Trump nominees, I think it is slim to none that we would support a nominee from this administration,” Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., a member of the Judiciary Committee, told NBC News in an interview before the elections. “Because we’ve seen this movie, we know how it ends, which is a politician in robes who is following Trump’s orders on most major questions.” Looking ahead, the election results could recast the fight for the Republican presidential nomination in 2028. The presumed GOP front-runner is Vice President JD Vance. But if the outcome amounts to a rejection of Trump and his brand of politics, Vance may find that he has no glide path to the nomination. As the minority party, Democrats lacked the power to issue subpoenas and schedule oversight hearings. That all changes come January, when the new Congress convenes. Democratic lawmakers are already signaling that they will look to rein in the spending and war-making powers Trump has wielded with little pushback from a compliant Republican-led Congress. House Democrats have vowed to carry out aggressive oversight of Trump’s family, business dealings and administration, including the ICE and Homeland Security immigration crackdown and Trump’s pet renovation projects at the White House and other Washington-area landmarks. At the tip of the spear of the investigations are Reps. Robert Garcia of California, the top Democrat on the Oversight Committee, and Jamie Raskin of Maryland, the top Democrat on the Judiciary Committee. Garcia has outlined his investigation strategy, focusing on what he calls “Trump family corruption,” including how Trump’s fortune has grown by billions of dollars since his 2024 campaign, as well as Jeffrey Epstein’s crimes and Trump’s immigration crackdown. Judiciary Committee Democrats said they also have a long list of investigative targets that includes pardons for “wealthy criminals and MAGA loyalists,” and foreign governments’ “buying influence” through gifts and payments to the Trump family’s crypto empire . Jeffries has said that Democrats aren’t focused on impeaching Trump but that they also haven’t ruled it out. Trump was impeached twice during his first term but acquitted both times by the Senate. “The cost of living is way too high, and Donald Trump — along with his Republican sycophantic members of Congress — have actually decided not to do anything about it because so many of them are so focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends and their donors. There is a cost to corruption,” Jeffries told reporters before the election. “These are all things that are going to need to be thoroughly investigated as part of our pledge to hold the crooks accountable, beginning on day one,” he said. Given the election results, Republicans may be motivated to usher in pieces of their legislative agenda during the lame-duck session before they officially relinquish control of the House on Jan. 3. They could include another party-line “reconciliation” bill to advance Trump’s spending and tax priorities, along with a debt ceiling increase before a 2027 deadline. The political future of Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., is unknown. He would need a majority of the Senate GOP caucus in a closed-ballot election to carry on as minority leader. But he has had an up-and-down relationship with Trump, who has vented frustration with him for failing to eliminate the filibuster to pass the SAVE America Act, which would overhaul the country’s election laws. Another mystery is the fate of Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., who has run the House for the past three years. He could stay on as minority leader, but in the face of the defeat across the board, some rank-and-file Republicans are likely to demand new leadership.

items.title: Teachers in Peshawar protest ‘abrupt layoffs’ by UNHCR
items.description: PESHAWAR: Hundreds of Pakistani teachers, who provided education to Afghan children in refugee camps for decades, but were laid off without any financial relief, protested here on Tuesday against the ‘abrupt’ layoffs. As many as 291 teachers, who have been providing education to Afghan children under the auspices of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) for the past 35 to 40 years, have been laid off without prior notice or any financial relief. The affected teachers, including 100 men and 191 women, were reportedly dismissed from service on Oct 31. They belong to Peshawar, Mardan, Timergara, Nowshera, Swabi, Haripur, Kohat, Dera Ismail Khan, Bannu, Lakki Marwat, Hangu, Tall, Chakdara, and Jalala Shergarh. The dismissed teachers demanded compensation and financial relief for their decades of service. The protest was led by Tufail Ahmed and Farhana Durrani, who heads the women teachers. Addressing the protesters, Mr Ahmed said they had devoted nearly four decades of their lives to educating Afghan children in refugee camps but had been dismissed through a single administrative decision without any notice or relief. He said the teachers had already been deprived of medical allowances, other financial benefits and gratuity despite serving in schools established in Afghan refugee camps for decades. “We served the institution for four decades, but were sent home at the stroke of a pen without any compensation or relief,” he said. On the occasion, Ms Durrani said she had spent 35 years teaching Afghan children and had worked tirelessly to fulfil her responsibilities. “After 35 years of dedicated service, the UNHCR sent us home through a single phone call, without providing any financial relief,” she said. The protesters said the sudden termination of their employment had pushed hundreds of families into severe financial difficulties, with many struggling to meet even their basic household expenses. They complained that despite repeatedly visiting the UNHCR office to present their grievances, no official was willing to hear them or engage in dialogue. They further alleged that instead of addressing their concerns, the office had closed its doors to them and deployed police personnel outside, with protesters being warned of a possible baton charge. They appealed to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi to intervene and play his role in securing relief for the affected teachers and their families. A large number of young and elderly women teachers also participated in the sit-in, demanding recognition of their decades-long services and financial assistance following their dismissal. Published in Dawn, November 4th, 2026
