items.title: Govt unveils LPG policy as power costs set to rise
items.description: • Directs four SOEs to re-enter LPG import business • Plans subsidised LPG at Rs300-350 per kg for BISP-eligible consumers ISLAMABAD: The government on Tuesday directed four state-owned enterprises (SOEs) to re-enter the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) import business to ease severe supply constraints and soaring prices, while the power division sought an estimated Rs2-4 per unit increase in electricity purchase costs for the next calendar year. Speaking at a news conference at PTV headquarters, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said the federal cabinet had approved a broad-based LPG policy aimed at creating competition and supplies through procurement by four SOEs under government-to-government (G2G) and business-to-business (B2B) arrangements. He acknowledged that LPG, often described as the poor man’s fuel, was in short supply even before the onset of winter because of disruptions along the western borders. As a result, unscrupulous elements were selling LPG at Rs700-800 per kg, depending on the area, against the maximum price of Rs295 per kg notified by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) for November, he said. “Looking at the Saudi CP (Contract Price) rate and prevailing premiums, its local price in the market would be Rs450-500 per kg” once supplies from SOEs began, the minister said. He added that private-sector importers would remain free to arrange supplies at lower rates to compete. Mr Malik said the prime minister had directed that LPG be provided to deserving and vulnerable consumers at Rs300-350 per kg, using the eligibility criteria of the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP). The subsidy would be financed through a new account funded by the difference between the LPG import parity price and proceeds from auctions of locally produced LPG supplied by refineries and exploration and production companies, under a clawback mechanism. The minister told Dawn that the four SOEs — Pakistan State Oil, Pakistan LNG Ltd, Sui Sout­hern Gas-LPG and Parco-LPG — had already received offers for LPG supplies from Saudi Arabia and Oman. However, even the proposed subsidised price of Rs300-350 per kg for BISP-eligible consumers would exceed Ogra’s current notified maximum price of Rs294.08 per kg. Power purchase costs Separately, a power division team presented six scenarios for rebasing the power purchase pr­ice (PPP) for January-Dece­m­ber 2027 at a public hearing cond­u­cted by the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra). Industrial consumers criticised the government for creating additional entities and hiring staff at exorbitant salaries, arguing that these costs were contributing to higher electricity tariffs. Central Power Purchasing Agency CEO Rehan Akh­tar and Power Planning and Monitoring Company CFO Naveed Qaiser presented the projections, all of which put next year’s power purchase price, excluding taxes and other charges, above this year’s Rs25.32 per unit. None of the scenarios assumed that the US-Iran war would continue into 2027. Under the base-case scenario, the power purchase price was projected at Rs27.31 per unit, an increase of Rs1.99. The ideal scenario, which officials acknowledged was unlikely to materialise, projected Rs25.883 per unit, up Rs0.563. The two worst-case scenarios put the price at Rs28.84 and Rs29.26 per unit, representing increases of Rs3.52 and Rs3.94, respectively. Two other scenarios, involving changes in electricity demand and greater LNG and natural gas availability, projected increases of Rs2.25 and Rs1.12 per unit. Nepra reserved its decision and will issue its determination after examining the record and submissions. The projected annual power purchase cost ranges from Rs3.4 trillion to Rs3.8tr. Explaining the new LPG policy, Mr Malik said the Competition Commission of Pakistan, the National Explosives and Petroleum Safety Agency and Ogra had been tasked with addressing collusive practices, quality standards and price monitoring in coordination with district administrations. He said the quota system benefiting influential groups would be abolished, while local producers would auction LPG in lots of five to 10 tonnes through a competitive process monitored by Ogra and the petroleum division. Under the new arrangement, SOEs would import LPG in bulk and publish the base price, linked to the Saudi Aramco Contract Price. These would be disclosed on their websites as the monthly average landed cost. Ogra would cease issuing price notifications for locally produced and imported LPG. Local producers would receive the producer price determined through auctions, while the difference between the producer price and the SOE-linked base price would be deposited in a fund to subsidise LPG for BISP-eligible consumers. Published in Dawn, November 4th, 2026

items.title: Experts seek soil-based fertiliser recommendations to improve yields
items.description: By Cynthia Alo Agricultural experts have called for a shift from one-size-fits-all fertiliser recommendations to soil-based application, warning that farmers may be wasting money on nutrients their crops do not need. They said differences in soil conditions and crop requirements meant that applying the same fertiliser rates across farming locations could result in poor nutrient use, higher production costs and lower productivity. The experts spoke at the 2026 Nigeria Fertiliser Summit on Phosphorus and Food Security, organised by the Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T), Obafemi Awolowo University and the Fertilizer Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN), with the Fertilizer and Inputs Support Services Department of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security as co-convener in Abuja. Findings presented at the summit by the Regional Hub for Fertilizer and Soil Health for West Africa and the Sahel showed that phosphorus requirements for maize and rice in northern Nigeria ranged from zero to more than 60 kilogrammes of phosphorus pentoxide per hectare, depending on soil conditions. Phosphorus is an essential plant nutrient that supports root development, crop growth and grain formation. However, its availability to crops varies with soil properties and farming conditions. A soil scientist and modelling expert at IAR&T, Prof. Vincent Aduramigba-Modupe, said improving agricultural productivity required more than increasing fertiliser application. “Improving crop productivity is not only about applying fertiliser. It is about ensuring the right nutrient is applied in the right amount, at the right place, and under the right conditions,” he said. The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Aliyu Abdullahi, represented by the Director of Agricultural Land and Climate Change Management Services, Oshadiya Olanipekun, emphasised soil data, testing and crop-specific fertiliser recommendations as important tools for improving farmers’ outcomes. Also speaking, Prof. Jibrin Mohammed Jibrin, Visiting Scientist with the Regional Hub and Professor of Soil Science at Bayero University, Kano, described soil information as fundamental to food production. Jibrin also called for better coordination among agricultural stakeholders, warning that fragmented interventions could undermine efforts to improve soil health. “The basis of food production and food security is the soil. You need healthy soil to produce well and feed the nation with nutritious food. To do that, you need soil intelligence. “Too many initiatives have been implemented in silos. Real progress will come when stakeholders align, collaborate and follow through on agreed actions,” he said. Senior Agronomist at the Regional Hub, Dr. Bello Shehu, said improving phosphorus management was not about applying more fertiliser but understanding the nutrient requirements of different soils and crops. The Vice-Chancellor of Obafemi Awolowo University, Prof. A.S. Bamire also stressed that agricultural productivity depended on responsible nutrient management, research, innovation and stronger partnerships. items.title: No cover-up for NDC wrongdoers; Mahama will protect no one – Fifi Kwetey
items.description: NDC General Secretary Fifi Fiavi Kwetey says President John Mahama will shield no one who engages in wrongdoing, including members of the governing party. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, he warned that party membership would offer no protection from accountability. “And I can tell you, the president is not going to cover anyone. We are not going to set up any scheme to try to cover nobody.” Mr Kwetey said the strongest test of the NDC’s commitment to accountability would be its willingness to punish its own members. “So, as far as I’m concerned, the real, the real punishment is not the punishment meted out to an NPP person. The real punishment is the one meted out to somebody in the NDC.” His comments come amid scrutiny over the World Cup visa scandal and sexual abuse allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School. President Mahama suspended National Sports Authority Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah on October 1 over alleged World Cup visa racketeering. Police investigations followed, alongside a presidential committee inquiry. Mr Ankrah has denied wrongdoing. In the Obuasi case, the NDC initially directed headmaster Zakaria Abdulai to withdraw from its Juaben chairmanship race. It briefly cleared him to contest before directing him to step aside on October 20 to allow an unhindered police investigation. The party stressed that the decision did not establish guilt. Mr Kwetey argued that the NDC must hold itself to a higher standard. He linked that responsibility to the executions associated with the party’s political origins. “So you can’t be in NDC and expect that you do the same thing NPP does and expect the party to cover you. No, there’s no cover-up.” He also cautioned members against treating electoral victory as proof that the party was exceptional. He said voters had rejected the NPP’s conduct, and repeating it would threaten the NDC’s future. For him, the decisive issue was how the government responded when wrongdoing emerged. “But the way you deal with them is what matters.” He insisted that the party was prepared to discipline its members and make examples of those who failed to uphold the required standards. “If you are not capable of doing what is right. Other people would take that position and do it.”

items.title: What Is It About Jon Ossoff?
items.description: When Jon Ossoff was first elected, in January 2021, he felt a little like an accidental senator. He was 33 years old and had won by just 55,000 votes, defeating the unpopular Republican incumbent, David Perdue, in a runoff election overshadowed by President Trump’s bogus claims of voter fraud. He doesn’t feel accidental anymore. Ossoff cruised to reelection tonight. The final margin of victory is not yet known, but networks called the race early; soon after the polls closed, any drama was gone, even though he had been campaigning in a state that is barely purple. His triumph does not change much about the Senate’s electoral calculus overall, because Democrats were expected to hold his seat, but the decisive victory immediately propels him into the top ranks of the party and any discussions about the 2028 presidential contest. Ossoff’s win is a testament to his deftness as both senator and candidate. In office, he has emphasized constituent services but also mastered the art of getting under the skin of Republican officials during Senate hearings, without ever seeming ruffled himself. On the stump, his campaign showed an acute sense of how to use media, even producing a new coinage— the “Ossoff angle” —to describe the upward camera perspective that his team worked to produce. He paired these good visuals with a knack for the sound bite. In the most famous instance, in August, he slyly said that Trump “doesn’t want to do the job. He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie.” Although he omitted her last name, the moment made the president’s assistant Natalie Harp—who was previously familiar only to political reporters and political junkies—into a prominent figure. The ensuing news cycle was both damaging and distracting to the White House. As the youngest senator, Ossoff has shown a mastery of short-form video that few of his peers can dream of. Like many other Democrats this cycle, Ossoff benefited from the president’s unpopularity, disastrous agenda, and lack of political focus. He was running in a state that Trump had won by barely two points in 2024. Ossoff was also very lucky in his opponent. After failing to recruit a stronger candidate, Republicans landed on Mike Collins, whose many connections to white nationalists, including his son-in-law, helped sink him. But Ossoff made some of his own luck by intimidating better candidates into not running. He also showed a killer instinct on debate stages, savaging Collins over his ties to racists. Ossoff’s campaign was impressive enough that his name is on the lips of what the columnist Russell Baker called “ The Great Mentioner ,” the rumor mill of possible candidates for president. During the campaign, Ossoff promised to finish his next term as senator if he were reelected. “I have zero interest in running for president,” he said during a debate. “I’m not running for president. I’m running for reelection to the Senate.” But candidates who wish to do so have squirmed their way out of stronger commitments. What an Ossoff presidential campaign might look like is unclear. He resides more on the moderate wing of the party than on the left, but he does not have a strong ideological profile, and he has avoided confrontations with more progressive Democrats. To become a major national figure, he’ll have to define himself more clearly. And although in many ways the 2028 cycle has already begun, that election is a long way off in political time. The skills required to run for president are also on a different tier from those needed to win at the state level, as many senators and governors have learned the hard way in the past. Ossoff’s talent outside of carefully packaged media has not yet been demonstrated on the national level. One of the backhanded compliments he gets is that someone so good at direct-to-social video messaging can’t possibly be as charismatic one-on-one. His triumph tonight guarantees that he’ll instantly be in heavy demand on television and at Democratic events across the country, where he’ll have a chance to test and hone those skills.

items.title: Tour du Faso : Le burkinabè Saturnin Yameogo soulève la population de Pâ
items.description: Le Burkina Faso vient d’avoir sa première victoire d’étape ce mardi 03 novembre 2026 à Pâ. C’est Saturnin Yameogo qui franchit la ligne d'arrivée. Il a fait les 131,32 km en 2h48mn06s, avec une vitesse moyenne de 46,872 km/h. Le peuple burkinabè attendait une victoire d’étape. Certains la voyais la veille lors du critérium à Bobo-Dioulasso. Mais c’est finalement l’étape Bobo-Dioulasso-Pâ, que la victoire arrive. Ils sont 73 coureurs au départ ce matin dans la capitale économique pour cette 5 e étape. À Sogossagasso, le Burkinabè Vincent Mouni est victime d’une chute. Il signe abandon et ne pourra plus aider ses coéquipiers. Dans cette localité, le 1 er sprint intermédiaire intervient. Michel Boris TIENCHEU du Cameroun passe en 1 er . Tiémoko DIAMOUNTENE du Mali et Yacine HAMZA de l’Algérie sont respectivement 2 e et 3 e . Une échappée est lancée. Ils sont cinq (05) dont Saturnin Yameogo. Ils arrivent à posséder une avance de 3mn10s sur le peloton. À Koumbia au 2 e sprint intermédiaire, Saturnin Yameogo du Burkina Faso passe le 1 er . Il est suivi de Philip Heijnen des Pays-Bas et de Michel Boris Tiencheu du Cameroun. À Houndé pour le 3 e sprint intermédiaire, c’est Saturnin Yameogo qui passe. Adil El Arbaoui du Maroc est 2 e et Jannes Van Weele des Pays-Bas, 3 e . Les cinq (05) hommes de tête sont toujours devant et ils ne sont pas rattrapés. À trois (03) km de l’arrivée, ils sont à 1mn40s du peloton. Et c’est sans surprise que le sprint final se joue entre les fuyards. Le Burkinabé Saturnin Yameogo est fort dans le dernier coup de pédales. Il devance Abdellah Oussama Mimouni et Adil El Arbaoui. Cette victoire était, tant attendu que le public l'a porté en triomphe, avec des cris de joie. Il aurait fallu attendre la 5 e étape pour enfin voir une victoire d’étape burkinabè. Au classement général, le maillot jaune est toujours sur les épaules du Sud Africain Gustav Basson. Soumaila Ilboudo du Burkina Faso est 2 e à 41 secondes du leader du peloton. Timmy De Boes Belgique est 3 e à 44 secondes du Sud Africain. La caravane passe la nuit à Ouagadougou. Demain mercredi et pour la 6 e étape, elle quitte Saponé pour Léo, chef lieu de la province de la Sissili. items.title: NDC risks digging its own grave by repeating NPP’s mistakes – Fifi Kwetey
items.description: NDC General Secretary Fifi Fiavi Kwetey has warned that the party risks digging its own grave if it repeats the mistakes voters rejected under the NPP. Speaking on JoyNews’ PM Express on Tuesday, he urged the governing party to remain humble. He said its victory reflected the public’s rejection of the NPP rather than any special entitlement to power. “Now, so when you come and try to repeat what the NPP does, you are literally just digging your own grave.” He warned members against treating party membership or government office as protection from accountability. “Those days must be a thing of the past.” Mr Kwetey said the party’s commitment to discipline would be tested most clearly by its willingness to punish its own members. “The real punishment is the one meted out to somebody in the NDC.” His warning comes amid the alleged World Cup visa scandal involving the National Sports Authority. Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah was suspended, and police are investigating the matter. He has denied wrongdoing. The NDC has also faced scrutiny over its handling of sexual abuse allegations against Obuasi Senior High Technical School headmaster Zakaria Abdulai. The party initially ordered him to withdraw from its Juaben constituency chairmanship contest. It then allowed him to proceed, citing fairness and the presumption of innocence, before directing him to step aside again. The allegations remained under investigation. Mr Kwetey insisted that the NDC must hold itself to a higher standard. He linked that obligation to executions associated with the party’s political origins. “So you can’t be in NDC and expect that you do the same thing NPP does and expect the party to cover you. No, there’s no cover-up.” He said wrongdoing could occur in any institution. What mattered was how those in charge responded. “But the way you deal with them is what matters.” He also pledged that President John Mahama would not shield anyone, saying, “And I can tell you, the president is not going to cover anyone.” For party members unwilling to uphold the required standards, his message was blunt: “If you are not capable of doing what is right. Other people would take that position and do it.”

items.title: Drame passionnel à Tenkodogo : Course-poursuite, tirs mortels et suicide, la fin tragique d’un couple entre une commerçante et un sous-officier FDS
items.description: La ville de Tenkodogo est plongée dans la stupeur et la consternation à la suite d'un drame nocturne survenu au secteur 6, non loin de la pharmacie de l’hôpital. Selon des témoignages de riverains recueillis par l’Agence d’information du Burkina (AIB), une violente dispute conjugale éclatée dans la nuit du 1ᵉʳ au 2 novembre 2026 entre deux fiancés s'est achevée dans un bain de sang. Jeanne Yoda, commerçante, a été mortellement touchée par arme à feu après avoir été prise en chasse par son compagnon, Adama Tiendrébéogo, sous-officier des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), qui aurait ensuite retourné l'arme contre lui. Tous deux sont décédés des suites de leurs blessures au Centre hospitalier régional (CHR) de Tenkodogo, laissant le voisinage sous le choc dans l'attente des conclusions des enquêtes officielles. La quiétude de la ville carrefour du Centre-Est a basculé dans l’épouvante au cours de la nuit du dimanche 1ᵉʳ au lundi 2 novembre 2026. D'après les éléments rapportés par l’Agence d’information du Burkina (AIB) auprès du voisinage immédiat, les faits ont débuté aux abords de la pharmacie de l’hôpital. Une dispute d’une vive intensité s’est déclenchée entre Jeanne Yoda, commerçante de la place, et Adama Tiendrébéogo, sous-officier au sein des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS). Présentés par les habitants du quartier comme un couple uni depuis près de deux ans et activement engagé dans les préparatifs de leur mariage, les deux tourtereaux en sont pourtant rapidement venus aux mains. Malgré l'intervention de riverains accourus pour tenter de séparer les protagonistes et apaiser la querelle physique, l'escalade n'a pu être évitée. La dispute a alors pris une tournure dramatique dès lors que la jeune femme a cherché à fuir l’emprise de la violence. Selon les récits concordants des témoins cités par l’AIB, Jeanne Yoda est montée sur son scooter afin de regagner rapidement son domicile. Déterminé à ne pas en rester là, son compagnon s'est lancé à sa poursuite avant de faire usage d'une arme à feu dans des circonstances qui restent à éclaircir. Atteinte de plein fouet et grièvement blessée par les tirs, la commerçante a été évacuée d’urgence vers le Centre hospitalier régional (CHR) de Tenkodogo, situé à proximité. Malheureusement, la gravité de ses lésions n'a laissé aucune chance au corps médical : son décès a été constaté peu de temps après son admission aux urgences. Dans la foulée de ces tirs, l'agresseur présumé a scellé son propre sort. Toujours selon les témoignages rapportés par l'agence de presse nationale, le sous-officier des FDS aurait retourné l'arme contre lui-même. Évacué à son tour dans un état critique au sein du même établissement hospitalier régional, l'homme a finalement succombé à ses blessures dans l’après-midi du lundi 2 novembre 2026. Cette double perte brutale plonge la communauté locale dans une incompréhension totale, d'autant qu'un voisin ayant requis l'anonymat soulignait qu'Adama Tiendrébéogo venait régulièrement prêter main-forte à sa fiancée dans sa boutique en dehors de ses heures de service. Si l'émotion reste particulièrement vive dans le quartier, de nombreuses zones d'ombre demeurent suspendues aux investigations légales. L'AIB a précisé qu'aucune communication officielle émanant des autorités sécuritaires ou judiciaires n’avait encore été rendue publique au moment de la relation des faits. Les circonstances exactes de l'altercation, le mobile précis du passage à l'acte, la trajectoire des secours ainsi que la nature de l’arme employée — notamment pour déterminer s'il s'agissait ou non d'une arme de dotation réglementaire devront être formellement établies par les enquêtes diligentées par les services compétents. items.title: Tragédie dans un grin à Bobo-Dioulasso : Une dispute autour d’un partage de nourriture vire au meurtre sauvage
items.description: L’intolérance et la rancœur ont conduit à l’irréparable au secteur 15 (Ouezzinville) de Bobo-Dioulasso. Ce lundi 2 novembre 2026, lors d'un point de presse animé dans les locaux du Commissariat de police de l’arrondissement de Dafra, les autorités policières ont levé le voile sur les circonstances effroyables d’un assassinat né d'une simple dispute autour du partage d’un repas au sein d'un « grin ». Après plusieurs altercations avortées, le présumé meurtrier, un homme de 52 ans, a guetté sa victime le 18 octobre dernier pour lui asséner un coup fatal de bâton avant de la mutiler à l'aide d'un tesson de bouteille brisé sur place. Évacuée d'urgence au Centre médical urbain (CMU) de Ouezzinville, la victime a succombé à de profondes blessures à la tête et aux bras. Désormais passé aux aveux, le mis en cause devra répondre de ses actes devant le Procureur du Faso. Le traditionnel espace de convivialité et d'échanges qu'est le « grin » a été le théâtre d'une rancune mortelle. Réunis ce lundi 2 novembre 2026 dans l’enceinte du Commissariat de Police de l’arrondissement de Dafra, le Commissaire central de police de la ville de Bobo-Dioulasso, Soumaïla Nombré, et le Commissaire principal de police Idrissa Sawadogo, responsable dudit commissariat, ont exposé les résultats de plusieurs enquêtes criminelles. Si des réseaux d'escroquerie mystique transfrontalière et de recel d'engins ont été démantelés, c’est le dénouement tragique d'un meurtre avec préméditation commis dans les environs du Centre médical urbain (CMU) de Ouezzinville, au secteur 15, qui a particulièrement glacé l'assistance. À l’origine de ce drame, un motif d'une futilité déconcertante qui a fini par empoisonner les relations entre deux habitués du grin. Selon les explications détaillées fournies par les enquêteurs, une vive altercation avait éclaté entre la victime et le présumé meurtrier, un quinquagénaire âgé de 52 ans, au sujet du partage d’un repas consommé en groupe. Cette friction initiale avait rapidement dégénéré en haine tenace. Par deux fois, des bagarres avaient failli éclater entre les deux hommes lors de séances ultérieures au grin, mais la vigilance et la médiation des autres membres présents avaient permis, temporairement, d'éviter le pire. L’accalmie n'était malheureusement qu'illusoire. Le 18 octobre 2026, à la suite d'un nouveau différend écourté de justesse par les pairs du grin, le mis en cause a décidé de passer à l’acte de façon méthodique. Profitant du fait que son rival reprenait seul son chemin après l'incident, le quinquagénaire s'est lancé à ses trousses. Bien qu’ayant une machette à sa portée, l'agresseur a délibérément choisi un mode opératoire d'une violence inouïe. Muni d'un gourdin, il a d'abord rattrapé et assommé sa cible par surprise. Alors que la victime gisait au sol en totale position de faiblesse, le forcené a brisé une bouteille sur les lieux pour s’emparer d'un tesson tranchant, s'acharnant sur le malheureux. Les coups répétés ont causé de profondes et larges lacérations au niveau de la tête et des bras. Transportée d'urgence au Centre médical urbain de Ouezzinville situé non loin, la victime a rendu l'âme peu de temps après son admission. Les investigations méticuleuses enclenchées par les services de recherche de Dafra ont rapidement permis de remonter la piste de l'agresseur. Interpellé et confronté aux éléments matériels recueillis par la police, le suspect de 52 ans est passé sans détour aux aveux, décrivant avec précision l’enchaînement de son passage à l'acte. Il sera très prochainement déféré et présenté devant le Procureur du Faso près le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Bobo-Dioulasso pour répondre formellement de l'inculpation d'assassinat. Ce drame absurde remet au premier plan la question de la gestion pacifique des conflits au sein des espaces de socialisation de quartier. En marge de la présentation des faits, les commissaires Soumaïla Nombré et Idrissa Sawadogo ont lancé un appel pressant aux populations burkinabè, les exhortant à cultiver la tolérance, le dialogue et la retenue mutuelle afin d’éviter que des désaccords mineurs ne virent au bain de sang. Les responsables de la police ont également réitéré l’importance de la vigilance citoyenne, rappelant à tous les numéros verts gratuits — le 17 (Police nationale), le 16 (Gendarmerie nationale) et le 1010 (Centre national de veille et d'alerte) — pour dénoncer tout comportement suspect ou velléité d’agression avant qu'un drame ne soit consommé. items.title: GIS trains 146 officers to strengthen firearms accountability
items.description: The Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) has trained 146 officers in weapon safety and armoury management in a move to strengthen accountability in the handling, storage and tracking of firearms and ammunition. The two-day seminar, held at the Ghana Immigration Centre of Excellence in Accra on 28th and 30th October 2026, brought together regional and selected sector commanders for practical training in the safe handling, storage, issuance and tracking of weapons. The programme was organised in collaboration with armoury management experts from the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF), the Ghana Police Service (GPS) and the Small Arms Commission of Ghana. Speaking at the opening ceremony, Comptroller-General of Immigration, Mr Samuel Basintale Amadu, described the training as a timely intervention to protect officers, safeguard state-owned weapons, prevent the loss of firearms and ammunition, and sustain public confidence in the Service. He urged participants to apply the knowledge and skills acquired to improve practices within their respective commands, stressing that proper weapon management was fundamental to professionalism, discipline and operational readiness. The Armourer General of the Ghana Police Service, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCOP) Isaac K. Asante, highlighted the risks associated with weak inventory controls, poor record-keeping and inadequate supervision of weapons. He urged Regional and Sector Commanders to maintain accurate registers, conduct regular inspections and enforce strict procedures for the issuance and return of firearms and ammunition. DCOP Asante emphasised that every weapon and round of ammunition must be accounted for and traceable to a responsible officer at all times. Lieutenant Colonel Frank Tetteh-Kumah, Commander of the 851 Ammunition and Explosives Ordnance Regiment of the Ghana Armed Forces, also took participants through standard operating procedures governing military armoury management. He encouraged the Immigration Service to adopt relevant aspects of the military’s systems, particularly in physical security, access control, documentation, routine audits and command-level accountability. A delegation from the Small Arms Commission, led by its Director of Operations, Emmanuel Felix Mantey, facilitated sessions on stockpile management and firearm safekeeping. The sessions addressed measures to prevent weapon diversion, restrict unauthorised access, improve storage conditions and ensure proper tracking of firearms throughout their lifecycle. The Head of Intelligence of the Ghana Immigration Service, Deputy Commissioner of Immigration (DCOI) Kwasi Opoku Apau, described the seminar as timely, particularly in view of the Service’s expanding responsibilities in border and national security. He said building officers’ capacity in weapon safety and armoury management was essential to the Service’s ambition to become a model institution in migration and border management. The Ghana Immigration Service says the seminar is expected to improve compliance with weapon-safety procedures, strengthen supervision across Regional and Sector Commands and foster a stronger institutional culture of accountability in the management of firearms and ammunition.

items.title: Samuel Abu Jinapor writes on Tuesday’s incident in Parliament
items.description: At Tuesday’s sitting of Parliament, I raised serious and disturbing allegations concerning the alleged sale of Ghanaian diplomatic passports for amounts ranging from US$10,000 to US$50,000. In my capacity as Ranking Member of Parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration Committee, I called for the Minister for Foreign Affairs to appear before Parliament and account for these allegations. The Majority Leader objected to my intervention. However, I maintained that allegations of such gravity, already circulating in the public domain, cannot simply be ignored. They have serious implications for Ghana’s international reputation, the integrity of our diplomatic passports and the credibility of our institutions. As Ranking Member, I consider it my solemn duty to bring such consequential matters before Parliament, without fear or favour. I owe this duty to Ghana, my constituents and the New Patriotic Party. The Rt. Hon. Speaker, Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, subsequently directed me to withdraw the said statement. I have enormous respect for the Office of the Speaker and for Rt. Hon. Alban Bagbin personally. That respect, however, does not diminish my constitutional and parliamentary responsibility to raise matters of grave national concern and demand accountability. I am deeply grateful to my colleagues on the Minority side who stood firmly with me and walked out in solidarity when the Speaker directed that I be escorted out of the Chamber. Let me be clear: Respect for parliamentary authority and the pursuit of accountability are not mutually exclusive. I remain a disciplined, patriotic and respectful Member of Parliament, but equally a proud and committed member of the Mighty Minority, determined to hold the Government accountable, particularly in matters concerning our foreign affairs. Accountability is non-negotiable! God bless our homeland Ghana.

items.title: Traque contre la contrebande : La CNLF frappe un grand coup avec plus de 95 millions de FCFA de marchandises saisies
items.description: Dans une offensive coordonnée allant de Ouagadougou jusqu'à Diébougou, les agents de la Coordination Nationale de Lutte contre la Fraude (CNLF) ont démantelé un important réseau de contrebande. Ce coup de filet d'envergure a permis d'intercepter une cargaison hétéroclite de produits prohibés et de denrées alimentaires frauduleuses d'une valeur globale estimée à plus de 95 millions de FCFA. Entre saisies de substances hautement sensibles comme le cyanure, interception de carburant et blocage de 55 tonnes de riz de contrebande, les hommes du coordonnateur national, Dr Mohamadi Compaoré, réaffirment avec fermeté la primauté de la loi et la protection de l'économie nationale. La vigilance des services de contrôle vient de porter un coup rude aux circuits clandestins qui fragilisent le tissu économique. Au terme d’investigations minutieuses et d’interventions sur le terrain, la Coordination Nationale de Lutte contre la Fraude (CNLF) a mis hors d'état de nuire un système de contrebande ramifié s’étendant de la capitale jusqu’à Diébougou. Ce déploiement stratégique a abouti à une saisie globale évaluée à plus de 95 000 000 FCFA, témoignant de l'intensité du trafic déjoué. La diversité des produits interceptés illustre la dangerosité des filières neutralisées. Au-delà du préjudice financier causé au Trésor public, ce sont de véritables menaces sécuritaires et sanitaires qui ont été stoppées. Les agents de la CNLF ont notamment mis la main sur des stocks de cyanure — produit chimique hautement contrôlé —, ainsi que sur 14 000 litres de gasoil, des cargaisons d'huile alimentaire et d'importants lots de boissons illicites. À Diébougou, l’étau s’est également refermé sur 55 tonnes de riz issues de circuits frauduleux. Chaque interception vient préserver la santé des consommateurs tout en protégeant les opérateurs économiques respectueux des règles contre une concurrence déloyale délétère. Derrière l'ampleur de ces résultats chiffrés se trouve l'engagement soutenu d'agents de terrain mobilisés au quotidien au service de l'intérêt général. Saluant ce bilan opérationnel, le coordonnateur national de la CNLF, le Dr Mohamadi Compaoré, a tenu à adresser une mise en garde limpide aux auteurs d'activités illicites : la fraude ne trouvera aucune brèche. Cette action d'envergure réaffirme que la rigueur réglementaire et l'intégrité constituent le socle indispensable pour garantir la sécurité publique, sauvegarder la souveraineté de l'État et assainir durablement le marché national. items.title: SDA Church steps in to rescue overstretched Wa Municipal Hospital from environmental crisis
items.description: The Wa Municipal Hospital has received a critical environmental intervention from the Seventh-day Adventist (SDA) Church to combat health risks amid severe labour shortages at the facility. Members of the Wa Central and Peggrie Estate SDA churches dedicated their Sunday to an extensive weeding and sweeping operation across the hospital’s overgrown grounds. The Wa Central District Head Pastor, Pastor Whaley Asonre Aboungo, explained that the facility was specifically chosen because strict environmental hygiene is essential to protect vulnerable patients from preventable conditions like cholera. Citing biblical principles from Deuteronomy, Pastor Aboungo emphasised that cleanliness is a daily duty to God and humanity, noting that ignoring this civic responsibility is considered a sin. The church’s intervention highlighted the dire operational constraints facing the healthcare facility. Joseph Adongo, the Wa Municipal Hospital Administrator, revealed that the hospital currently has no dedicated outdoor labourers. Although the facility already carries over 100 casual workers on its payroll, management faces immense difficulty hiring additional grounds staff. Adongo explained that whenever interior cleaning or cooking staff resign, the hospital is forced to pull its outdoor contract laborers inside, leaving the exterior environment neglected. Expressing profound gratitude for the intervention, he appealed to other corporate bodies and religious organisations to emulate the SDA Church’s initiative to support their overstretched workforce. Local leaders are leveraging this event to advocate for broader, systemic changes to waste management across the municipality. Pastor Aboungo appealed directly to the President, regional ministers, and municipal chief executives to deploy public dustbins at strategic corners to actively discourage littering. Addressing the structural issues, Municipal Environmental Health Officer Kanyiti Razak urged a shift from a linear waste disposal system to a circular economy that treats waste as a resource. Mr Razak recommended that citizens practice strict waste segregation at the source to reduce the volume of refuse transported to final disposal sites, and he challenged local religious leaders to dedicate at least five minutes of their regular services to sanitation education. Moving forward, the SDA leadership plans to evaluate the uncompleted portions of the hospital grounds before deciding whether to return next month or redirect their ongoing community cleanup efforts to other public spaces, such as local markets.

items.title: Karachiites blast SSGC for failing to supply gas even during meal times
items.description: KARACHI: A severe gas crisis gripped the city on Tuesday, as residents in several parts woke up to an unpleasant shock in the morning to find no gas in their stoves, contrary to the assurance by the Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) that gas would be provided during meal timings. The situation was further complicated by multiple contradictory gas supply schedules attributed to SSGC that began circulating on social media from Monday. However, the utility did not issue any clear and consolidated statement until late Tuesday evening, adding to the confusion. For the past some years, consumers have not been getting round-the-clock gas supply and the utility has never bothered to officially notify them of a three-time gas supply schedule, except to say that gas would be supplied during meal times. However, complaints poured in from several parts of the city, including Hasan Square Gulshan-i-Iqbal, Liaquatabad, North Nazimabad, Nazimabad, Federal B Area, North Karachi, Gulistan-i-Jauhar, Malir, Korangi, Landhi, Orangi Town, Lyari, Saddar, PECHS, DHA and Clifton, where citizens said even the limited schedule was not even being honoured. In localities where it was available, the pressure was so low that stoves could not be lit. Varying gas schedules on social media deepen confusion as utility remains silent People came down heavily on the gas utility for not keeping them informed about the gas loadshedding in advance. “Why does SSGC not inform us? At least send an SMS or give a notice on TV. We are left to guess the schedule”, said Khalid Hussain from Liaquatabad. Farhan Qureshi from Gulistan-i-Jauhar said that social media was showing three different SSGC schedules, and the gas utility itself is silent. “This confusion is deliberate to hide their failure.” Shahida Bibi from North Karachi said that when gas did come, it was so low that it could not even boil water for tea. “My stove makes a noise but the flame is like a candle. What are we supposed to cook on this?” she asked. The outage also caused severe hardship for the women, elderly, patients and schoolchildren. A resident from PECHS summed up the public anger: “SSGC has made life hell for Karachiites. No gas, no pressure, no notice, no shame. They should be taken to court for this cruelty.” With kitchens shut, a heavy rush was witnessed at hotels, restaurants, tandoors and roadside eateries, particularly in the evening, as families had no option but to buy expensive food from outside. What has made the situation worse is the soaring price of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), which has become unaffordable for the common man, particularly the poor. Residents said that with no gas and skyrocketing LPG rates, they were left with no viable option for cooking. “LPG prices have gone through the roof. It is like a sword hanging over us. How can an ordinary person buy such an expensive fuel? SSGC has forced us to buy expensive LPG and now even that is out of reach,” said Irfan Ali from Orangi Town. Abdul Sattar from Korangi said: “I earn Rs1,200 a day. Yesterday, I spent Rs800 on naan and salan for my eight-member family because there was no gas. It is impossible for the poor to survive like this.” Citizens demanded that SSGC immediately clarify its official schedule, ensure its implementation, control LPG prices in coordination with the authorities concerned and establish a system of advance public notice. Despite repeated attempts, no official response was available from SSGC until late at night. Published in Dawn, November 4th, 2026

items.title: Solidarité : Issouf Kindo, un héros au secours des Burkinabè expulsés de Guinée
items.description: Alors que des ressortissants burkinabè expulsés de Guinée tentent de regagner leur pays dans des conditions difficiles, Issouf Kindo, orpailleur et soutien indéfectible de l’AES vivant en Guinée, a transformé sa maison en refuge pour accueillir ses compatriotes. Aujourd’hui, dépassé par l’ampleur des besoins, il lance un appel urgent aux sociétés de transport burkinabè. Depuis l’expulsion de nombreux orpailleurs, dont plusieurs ressortissants burkinabè, de Guinée, des images de compatriotes marchant sur de longues distances pour rejoindre le Burkina Faso ont circulé sur les réseaux sociaux. Contraints de trouver un moyen de rentrer chez eux, certains ont emprunté la route en direction du Mali, dans l’espoir de regagner leur pays. Mais pendant que certains affrontent les difficultés du voyage, d’autres peuvent compter sur la solidarité d’un compatriote. En Guinée, Issouf Kindo a décidé de ne pas rester les bras croisés. Lui-même orpailleur et résident dans ce pays, il a ouvert les portes de sa maison pour accueillir le maximum de Burkinabè en difficulté. Au fil des arrivées, son domicile s’est progressivement transformé en un véritable lieu de rassemblement, presque un camp de réfugiés, où se retrouvent des compatriotes en attente d’une solution pour rentrer au pays. Trois jours d’attente dans des conditions difficiles Ce mardi 3 novembre 2026, la situation semble particulièrement préoccupante. Dans un appel lancé aujourd’hui , Issouf Kindo sollicite l’aide des propriétaires de sociétés de transport burkinabè afin qu’ils dépêchent des cars pour récupérer les ressortissants bloqués devant son domicile. Selon son témoignage, des personnes sont basés sur place depuis trois jours. Elles manquent de nourriture, de repos et de conditions d’hygiène convenables. Face à cette foule grandissante, les moyens d’accueil et la capacité d’assistance de son foyer ne suffisent plus. La situation est devenue difficile à gérer pour celui qui, malgré ses moyens limités, tente de venir en aide à ses frères et sœurs burkinabè. Depuis le début de cette situation, Issouf Kindo aurait multiplié les démarches et les appels à l’aide auprès de différentes personnes, dans l’espoir de mobiliser suffisamment de soutien pour permettre à ses compatriotes de quitter cette situation précaire. Son dernier appel s’adresse particulièrement aux transporteurs burkinabè. L’objectif est clair : mobiliser des cars pour organiser le retour des personnes bloquées et leur permettre de retrouver leurs familles au Burkina Faso. Au-delà des moyens de transport, cette situation appelle également une mobilisation des bonnes volontés et des structures capables d’apporter une assistance alimentaire et logistique. Issouf Kindo a déjà posé un acte de solidarité en ouvrant sa maison. Il est désormais urgent que d’autres prennent le relais. Aujourd’hui, Issouf Kindo mérite d’être salué pour son engagement. Mais surtout, son appel mérite d’être entendu. Transporteurs burkinabè, bonnes volontés, personnes de bonne foi : nos compatriotes ont besoin de vous. Parce qu’en pareilles circonstances, aucun Burkinabè ne devrait être laissé seul. Source: Tiwana24 L’article Solidarité : Issouf Kindo, un héros au secours des Burkinabè expulsés de Guinée est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Govt weighs options to recover $800m from Etisalat
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The government is considering international arbitration against Etisalat over the outstanding $800 million payment from the sale of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL), along with its opportunity cost since 2008 and applicable damages. The matter was discussed at a joint meeting of the Senate standing committees on information technology and privatisation on Tuesday, where members were informed that the Office of the Attorney General for Pakistan (OAGP) had been directed to implement the federal cabinet’s decision under Rule 24 of the Rules of Business, 1973, at the earliest. However, senators from both committees expressed surprise that they were not given access to the sale purchase agreement (SPA) concerning the divestment of 26pc shares in PTCL, along with management control, to UAE-based Etisalat International Pakistan (EIP). The meeting was jointly chaired by Senator Dr Afnanullah Khan, chairman of the Senate Standing Committee on Privatisation, and Senator Palwasha Khan, chairwoman of the Senate Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunications. Cabinet asks attorney general’s office to prepare case for international arbitration At the outset, IT Secretary Zarrar Hasham Khan informed the committees that the agenda item concerning Etisalat’s outstanding $800m payment to the government was sensitive. He requested the chairpersons to ask all unauthorised persons, including media representatives, to leave the meeting, following which the proceedings were held in camera. However, after the meeting, some senators expressed annoyance that they, too, had not been provided details of the PTCL sale agreement. “The strange part is that we parliamentarians cannot handle information, but it is safe with the bureaucrats,” one senator remarked. “There has to be a law in this regard, and parliament should be informed about such sales of national assets rather than depending upon bureaucrats and officers,” the senator added. According to a briefing submitted by the Ministry of Privatisation, a copy of which is available with Dawn, the government sold 26pc shares in PTCL, along with management control, to Etisalat in 2005 for $2.59 billion. Of this amount, $1.76bn was received, while approximately $800m remains unpaid. The briefing said the payment was linked to the transfer of PTCL properties to the new management. Although 99pc of the properties had been transferred, 32 of the total 3,246 properties remained untransferred. Etisalat, which is now known as e&, has continued to withhold the outstanding $800m because of the non-transfer of these properties. The ministry said the government had made extensive efforts since 2015 to resolve post-privatisation issues, including the formation of several committees and negotiations with Etisalat for an amicable settlement. However, the dispute remained unresolved, prompting the government to constitute another committee in July 2026, headed by the adviser to the prime minister on privatisation. The committee included representatives of the ministries of IT and law and the OAGP. Considering the 20-year history of the dispute, the committee recommended that Pakistan consider international arbitration, as provided under the SPA, to recover the outstanding $800m, along with its opportunity cost since 2008 and applicable damages. It also recommended that the attorney general assess the strength of Pakistan’s case, its prospects of success and the associated legal implications. “If merits of the case permit to pursue international arbitration, prior to issuance of the Notice of Intent to Etisalat, the Attorney General should seek approval of the prime minister or the federal government,” the privatisation ministry’s briefing stated. The Privatisation Division informed the committees that a summary had subsequently been submitted to the federal cabinet. Published in Dawn, November 4th, 2026

items.title: Refinery audit may cut prices by Rs40-50/litre
items.description: KARACHI: Petroleum dealers have called for an immediate, transparent and comprehensive forensic audit of the country’s oil refineries, citing a sharp rise in sector profitability and saying that a review of their finances could allow cuts of Rs40-50 per litre in petroleum prices. According to Topline Securities, refinery sector profitability rose to Rs32.2bn in 1QFY27 from Rs1.6bn in 1QFY26 and Rs1.1bn in 4QFY26, mainly due to higher Gross Refining Margins (GRMs) amid the US-Iran war. PPDA Chairman Malik Khuda Bakhsh and senior leadership said the petroleum minister’s recent statement on extraordinary refinery profits confirmed concerns and reservations the association had previously raised. In a statement, PPDA representatives said that the association had repeatedly pointed out that certain refineries had earned unusually high profits, the impact of which had ultimately been borne by ordinary consumers. Sector earns Rs32.2bn in July-Sept, almost 20 times higher than Rs1.6bn a year ago They said the petroleum minister had recently revealed that refineries earned, in just three months, profits equivalent to what they would normally generate in an entire year. They described the disclosure as a serious concern and called for an independent, impartial examination of refinery profits, production costs, pricing mechanisms, and other financial matters to establish the facts. The PPDA representatives said the government should order a comprehensive forensic audit of the financial records, expenditures, crude oil procurement costs, production expenses and revenues generated from the sale of petroleum products by all oil refineries. They said such an audit would help establish the circumstances and basis on which refineries earned extraordinary profits and determine how much of the financial burden was directly or indirectly transferred to consumers. They further stated that the relief provided to consumers should not be portrayed as an additional financial burden on refineries. The PPDA leaders observed that consumers were already facing severe economic pressure due to inflation, high electricity and gas tariffs, rising transportation costs and increasing prices of essential commodities. In these circumstances, a genuine reduction in petroleum prices could provide substantial relief to the general public. They maintained that consulting only refineries and other relevant institutions when making important decisions on the petroleum sector was insufficient. Representation of petroleum dealers was equally essential to ensure balanced, practical and effective policies through consultation with all stakeholders. The government, they said, should make petroleum dealers an integral part of the policymaking process and benefit from their practical experience, recommendations and understanding of market conditions. Published in Dawn, November 4th, 2026

items.title: Ouagadougou : La PDS de l’arrondissement n°12 ordonne la libération des abords des avenues Pascal Zagré et Élie Saré sous quarante-huit heures
items.description: La présidente de la délégation spéciale de l'arrondissement n°12 de Ouagadougou, Zalisa Paré/Salambéré, a invité les habitants des secteurs 53 et 54 à libérer le domaine public le long des avenues Pascal Zagré et Élie Saré dans un délai de quarante-huit heures à compter du mercredi 4 novembre 2026, en prévision des festivités du 11 décembre 2026. Selon un communiqué daté du 3 novembre 2026, le défilé officiel et d'autres activités commémoratives se dérouleront sur l'avenue Pascal Zagré et ses environs, dans l'arrondissement n°12. Pour la réussite de l'événement, le comité national d'organisation du 11 décembre 2026 a arrêté plusieurs mesures. Celles-ci portent sur l'élagage des arbres et le nettoyage des devantures des concessions, ainsi que sur l'enlèvement des kiosques, étals, conteneurs, agrégats et de tout matériel obstruant le domaine public. Les panneaux publicitaires et les panneaux d'indication installés sur les avenues Pascal Zagré et Élie Saré devront également être retirés, qu'ils aient fait ou non l'objet d'une autorisation préalable. La présidente de la délégation spéciale invite les habitants des secteurs concernés, en particulier les riverains des deux avenues, à se conformer strictement à ces mesures dans le délai imparti. Passé ce délai, prévient le communiqué, la mairie de l'arrondissement n°12 se réserve le droit de recourir à tout moyen pour faire appliquer ces décisions. Soulignant l'importance de ces actions pour la réussite des festivités, l'autorité municipale a dit compter sur l'esprit citoyen et le sens du patriotisme des populations. items.title: Being named in FIR doesn’t preclude someone from govt service: FCC
items.description: • Bench distinguishes between ‘accusatory instrument’ and ‘judicially established culpability’ • Holds that character verification should be based on authentic, independently verifiable material rather than conjecture or suspicion • Calls on authorities to review recruitment policies ISLAMABAD: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) on Tuesday ruled that the mere registration of an FIR could not constitute perpetual disqualification from public employment, while underlining the need for uniform, transparent and constitutionally compliant standards for verification of antecedents in public recruitment. The directive came as a two-judge FCC bench, consisting of Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan and Justice Ali Baqar Najafi, took up an appeal filed by Abdul Latif against a May 22, 2025, judgement of the Lahore High Court’s Multan bench, which had rejected his plea. The petitioner had secured second position on the merit list for the post of driver constable in the Punjab Police Department, but was denied appointment on account of his previous involvement in a criminal case. Despite his acquittal on Oct 11, 2018, and the subsequent issuance of police character certificates showing no criminal record, his representation was rejected by the competent authority on Sept 2, 2024. Consequently, his writ petition and subsequent intra-court appeal were also dismissed by the high court. Authored by Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan, the judgement examined the pivotal question of whether the prior registration of a criminal case could constitute a subsisting disqualification warranting his exclusion from appointment, even though he was acquitted by a court of competent jurisdiction before the commencement of recruitment proceedings. The essential consideration was whether a previous criminal accusation, despite having culminated in an acquittal, could lawfully be perpetuated as an enduring impediment to public employment, notwithstanding the candidate’s successful selection on merit, the judgement noted. Any such determination must necessarily conform to the constitutional imperatives of legality, equality and procedural fairness, the verdict said. Making a distinction between the mere registration of an FIR and judicially established culpability, the judgement noted that the former was merely an accusatory instrument, and constituted neither proof nor a presumption of guilt. Once an accused had been acquitted by a competent court, the appointing authority could not disregard that adjudication or treat the underlying accusation as established misconduct, the judgement emphasised. The FCC also laid down guiding principles for competent federal and provincial authorities, stating that mere registration of an FIR would not, ipso facto, constitute disqualification from public employment. A judicial acquittal should receive due recognition, subject to an objective assessment of the candidate’s antecedents and suitability. The court further held that adverse character verification should be based on authentic and independently verifiable material rather than conjecture or suspicion. Following an acquittal, the criminal case should not be reflected adversely in the police character certificate. Where proceedings remained pending, only their pendency should be disclosed, without any presumption of guilt. The FCC also directed the competent authorities to review and harmonise their recruitment policies in accordance with these principles, subject to the applicable statutory framework. Administrative discretion could not be used to perpetuate an unproved criminal accusation as an indelible stigma or a perpetual impediment to public employment, the judgement said, adding that such safeguards were indispensable to preserving institutional integrity, public confidence and the rule of law. In its concluding order, the FCC set aside the high court judgement as well as the departmental decision excluding the petitioner from appointment. Published in Dawn, November 4th, 2026

items.title: UN body to review Pakistan’s progress on rights today
items.description: ISLAMABAD: A United Nations committee will review Pakistan’s efforts to implement the Interna­tional Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR) during its eighth session in Geneva on Wednesday. The Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (CESCR) is a body of 18 independent experts that monitors implementation of the ICESCR by its state parties. The covenant enshrines economic, soc­ial and cultural rights, for instance the rights to adequate food, adequate housing, education, health, social security, water and sanitation. This year the session is taking place at a significant moment - the 60th anniversaries of the ICESCR and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights. For six decades, these two covenants have served as the foundation of the inte­rnational human rights framework. Together, they affirmed that all human rights were universal, indivisible, interdependent and mutually reinforcing. Progress in one area could not be sustained without progress in the others, the UN says. The committee seeks to develop a constructive dialogue with state parties, determine whether the covenant’s norms are being applied, and assess how the implementation and enforcement of the covenant could be improved so all people can enjoy these rights in full. Barrister Aqeel Malik, the Minister of State for Law and Justice, will lead the Pakistan delegation to a session which will review the country’s second periodic report under the international covenant. The 11-member delegation inclu­des Tahir Andrabi, Pakistan’s Amb­a­ssador and Permanent Represen­tative, the secretary to the ministry of human rights, and Nayyab Ali, a consultant on transgender rights. In its periodic report, Pakistan submitted that it has made considerable progress in ensuring that human rights enshrined in the covenant are justiciable under the domestic legal order. The courts and administrative departments are empowered to take cognizance in case of breach of any rights mentioned in the covenant. Pakistan signed the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights in Nov 2004 and ratified it in April 2008. The report contains information regarding the implementation of Articles 1 to 15 of the covenant. Meanwhile, Amnesty Intern­ational is due to submit a briefing paper to the UN Committee on Econ­omic, Social and Cultural Rig­hts to coincide with Pakistan’s second periodic review under the ICESCR. In its briefing, Amnesty International clai­m­ed Pakistan has not taken “substantive steps” to incorporate the three fundamental rights into its domestic legislation as binding rights. Despite several amendments to the Constitution in the subsequent reporting period, no efforts were made to incorporate the three rights into the fundamental rights chapter, Amnesty said. Amnesty International has recommended that Pakistan incorporate the rights recognised under the covenant fully into domestic legislation and ensure their direct enforceability before all courts and tribunals. It called upon Islamabad to provide regular and mandatory training to judges, prosecutors, lawyers and public officials about implementation of the agreement. Published in Dawn, November 4th, 2026

items.title: Chinese scientists discover thickening ground ice in parts of warming Tibet

items.title: Bangladesh: Academics Allegedly Targeted for Supporting Hasina
items.description: Click to expand Image The University of Dhaka in Bangladesh, July 1, 2021. © 2021 Sony Ramany/NurPhoto via AP Photo (London) – Scores of academics and students at public universities in Bangladesh have been arbitrarily punished because of their alleged affiliation with former ruler Sheikh Hasina and her Awami League party, Human Rights Watch said today. Any action to punish persons for their peaceful beliefs or without ensuring due process would violate the rights to freedom of expression and association protected under international human rights law and reproduce abusive attempts under previous administrations to control political opinion and expression at Bangladesh’s public universities. “Bangladesh has a long history of political debate in its universities, and only autocrats should fear such discourse, not a government formed following student protests,” said Meenakshi Ganguly, deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Bangladesh needs to turn the page on the repression of the past, not repeat it whenever the ruling and opposition parties trade places.” The sanctions—dismissals, suspension, and teaching restrictions—focus on allegations that they were complicit in violence by Hasina’s Awami League government, which was toppled by student-led protests in 2024, allegations of other “subversive” activities in support of her party, or their alleged discrimination against students wearing Islamic clothing. Hundreds of students, allegedly Awami League members and supporters, are also being expelled, denying them their education rights. Human Rights Watch interviewed over a dozen affected teachers, examined university correspondence, and reviewed and analyzed a televised discussion and a video posted on social media. Interviews with teachers and students also confirmed expulsions, cancellation of exam certificates, or barring students from campus. According to media reports in August 2026, at least 404 more academics at 22 universities, who were part of a pro-Awami League Telegram messaging app group, have been put under investigation. “What is happening now is that the university authorities are targeting with false allegations the group of teachers who are aligned to the Awami League and did not support the 2024 student movement,” said a professor at a public university, who is not identified for security reasons. “We are not allowed to go take classes, we cannot do research work, we cannot do anything.” Hundreds of people were killed in a brutal police crackdown on the protests in July and August 2024, which forced Hasina to flee and paved the way for the return of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party to power following an election in February 2026. The activities of the Awami League were criminalized by an interim government in May 2025. For years, Bangladesh’s universities have been run in a partisan manner, employing and promoting academics close to the party in government and acting against supporters of other political parties. Starting in September 2024, the newly appointed authorities at Dhaka University, the country’s most prestigious university, ordered 44 academics to stop their work and restricted teaching assignments of another 25, without a transparent or credible disciplinary investigation. Subsequently, six of the academics were formally “temporarily suspended” following the findings of an inquiry committee, and similar investigations have now begun against another 14 teachers. At Bangladesh Agricultural University in Mymensingh, the authorities dismissed, suspended, or removed 12 academics and demoted or restricted the activities of another 34 after setting up an “investigation commission,” though this did not appear to comply with the university’s legally established disciplinary process. And in Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University in Dhaka, 12 academics have been temporarily suspended and another 10 removed from academic activities following an inquiry process that teachers said they were not allowed to attend, an apparent breach of the law covering academic discipline. Another 85 teachers were denied promotions. In all, over 20 public universities have been affected, Human Rights Watch found. In March 2025, Dhaka University temporarily suspended 126 students, and withheld their exam certificates, after a fact-finding committee said it had found photographic, video, or social media evidence that they had attacked peaceful protesters. Cases filed with the police allege that another 277 Awami League students were involved. The university authorities have taken no formal action against them, but students and teachers confirmed that they stay away from campus for fear of arrest. Many of those named deny any role in the violence, yet the university has not provided a forum for them to answer the allegations. Among the academics affected is Professor Mashiur Rahman, from the Dhaka University sociology department, who since 2017 was deputed as a vice-chancellor at another university. He was told to stop all academic and administrative work on September 25, 2024. The allegations against him include claims that during the protests he “directly opposed the movement, calling it illegal, baseless and irrational,” during a July 2024 television discussion, although a video of the broadcast, reviewed by Human Rights Watch, shows no such comment. Another allegation is that at the prime minister’s house on August 3, 2024, he “incited genocide.” However, this was a meeting set up by the University Grants Commission that all vice-chancellors had to attend, and he has told Human Rights Watch that no evidence has been provided to him showing that he made such a statement, which he denies. On August 31, 2026, the university authorities recommended permanently suspending him, which he is appealing. The allegations against the sanctioned teachers at the Bangladesh Agriculture University center on their participation in a pro-Awami League march on August 4, 2024, the day before Hasina fled the country. A report by a Commission of Inquiry set up by the university refers to the march as a “terrorist” procession. A video posted on Facebook by the Bangladesh Agricultural University Journalists’ Association on August 4, 2024, and analyzed by Human Rights Watch, shows a scene from the march. In the video, a group can be seen walking on the campus chanting slogans. No direct confrontations are visible. Professor Purba Islam from the Department of Pharmacology was suspended on August 4, 2025, for her “sloganizing” at the procession, alleging “support for the oppression, persecution and genocide committed by the fascist and autocrat Sheikh Hasina.” No evidence of her shouting slogans is visible in the video. Professor Yahia Khandoker, from the university’s Department of Animal Breeding and Genetics, was also suspended on August 4, 2025, accused of maintaining “on the university campus, a clear position in favor of Sheikh Hasina’s mass killing.” Throughout the whole protest period, he said, he was with his family in Dhaka, not at the university. The High Court has stayed his suspension, though the Attorney General’s Office is appealing. Three academics, two of them in prison, were convicted by the country’s International Crimes Tribunal on crimes against humanity charges, with another awaiting trial. “Any acts of revenge against people who peacefully supported the previous government would show that freedoms of speech and assembly are not protected,” Ganguly said. “Universities should be places where people are free to express their views, not places where support is enforced for the government of the day.”

items.title: Bobo Dioulasso: De faux marabouts escroquent près de 82 millions à des victimes
items.description: « Quand Dieu prépare le macabo, si tu es trop pressé, il retire ton morceau et te le donne. Mais il faudra gérer les démangeaisons en silence ». Ce proverbe Dioula trouve ton sens dans cette affaire qui abreuve les tchapalos de Bobo. En effet, sept honnêtes citoyens ont estimé qu’ils avaient suffisamment travaillé à la sueur de leur front. Du coup la bénédiction qu’un labeur sain et la patience produisent, eux, la voulaient tout de suite et maintenant. C’est là que sont entrés en jeu les petits génies du mal, qui par quelques tours de passe-passe bien répétés en coulisses, ont réussi à convaincre nos braves qu’ils étaient des guichets automatiques humains. Voyant la fortune à portée de mains, chacun des sept a versé une mise correspondant à son ambition. Malheureusement pour eux, ils n’avaient pas vérifié la côte qui s’est avérée désastreuse pour eux. Car les multiplicateurs avaient eux même besoin d’argent. Et une fois les dépôts encaissés, ils ont tenté de s’évaporer. La chance, c’est que leur magie n’a pas dépassé celle des éléments de la Brigarde Laabal et de la police, qui une fois informée du dossier, ont repéré la trace des charlatans. Pour l’heure, sur les 82 millions perçus, nul ne sait combien reste en poche. D’ailleurs, la tête pensante est toujours en cavale. Comme on dit chez le voisin, c’est conséquence qui conseille, Yako! Tiwana24 Elji RIM L’article Bobo Dioulasso: De faux marabouts escroquent près de 82 millions à des victimes est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Poni/Bouroum-Bouroum: Une femme retrouvée morte par pendaison
items.description: Une femme âgée d’environ 54 ans a été retrouvée morte, pendue à un arbre, dans un bosquet situé à proximité d’une voie, dans la matinée du mardi 3 novembre 2026, a constaté l’AIB sur place. Selon les témoignages recueillis auprès du frère de la défunte, la victime présentait des troubles mentaux et suivait un traitement médical. Alertés, les services compétents se sont rendus sur les lieux pour procéder aux constatations d’usage. La police, accompagnée d’un médecin, a effectué les vérifications nécessaires avant que le corps ne soit remis à la famille pour les funérailles. À ce stade, les circonstances exactes du décès ne sont pas encore établies. items.title: Ségou : une laborantine de 26 ans retrouvée morte dans un fossé entre Pelengana et Dialabougou
items.description: Le samedi 31 octobre 2026, aux environs de 16 h30 , le corps sans vie d'une femme a été découvert dans un fossé situé entre Pelengana et Dialabougou, à Ségou. La victime a été identifiée comme étant Safiatou Boré, âgée de 26 ans et originaire de Koutiala. Fille de Ousmane Boré et de feue Mahawa Goïta, elle exerçait comme laborantine au Cabinet médical Ségovien, situé à Sébougou, dans la ville de Ségou. Selon les informations recueillies, elle résidait au quartier ATT bougou. Une moto de type Jakarta noire a également été retrouvée à proximité du corps.La victime présentait de graves blessures à la tête. Alertés du drame, les éléments de la gendarmerie de Pelengana et ceux de la Protection civile de Ségou se sont rendus sur les lieux à 16 h 30 pour procéder à la récupération du corps. Ces éléments soulèvent de nombreuses interrogations sur les circonstances de ce décès. Toutefois, aucune conclusion ne peut être tirée à ce stade. Les circonstances exactes de sa mort, ainsi que les conditions dans lesquelles la moto a été retrouvée à proximité, restent à établir par les autorités compétentes. Radio Jamana L’article Ségou : une laborantine de 26 ans retrouvée morte dans un fossé entre Pelengana et Dialabougou est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Singapore Airlines says 46,000 booking records affected by Amadeus breach
items.description: Singapore Airlines said on Tuesday that ​a cybersecurity incident involving Amadeus, its reservation technology provider, may have affected about 46,000 booking records. The airline joins Cathay Pacific Airways , Japan Airlines, South Korea’s Asiana Airlines and others that have reported customer data was compromised in the Amadeus breach. Malaysia Airlines also said ​some of its customer information may have been ⁠affected Singapore’s flag carrier said that data exposed by ​the breach included customers’ names, booking reference numbers, travel ​itineraries and booking classes Information including email addresses, phone numbers, travel document details, and KrisFlyer membership numbers may also have been accessed ​for about 620 booking records, the company said It ​added that Amadeus confirmed that bank account or credit card information ‌had ⁠not been leaked and bookings were not modified Singapore Airlines said it was reaching out to affected customers with upcoming travel plans to change their booking reference ​numbers as ​a precaution The ⁠airline also confirmed that its IT systems were not breached Amadeus said it had become ​aware of a vulnerability affecting a travel ​booking ⁠display environment but did not respond to a question on how many customers’ data were affected In recent days, ⁠Cathay ​Pacific and Japan Airlines reported ​that the breach had affected data involving 53,000 bookings and 92,000 customers, ​respectively

items.title: NDC admits error in clearing Obuasi SHTS headmaster amid abuse allegations
items.description: The General Secretary of the NDC, Fifi Kwetey, has acknowledged that the party mishandled its initial response to sexual abuse allegations against the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), saying it should have waited for further evidence before taking a position. Zakaria Abdulai, the headmaster of Obuasi SHTS, was the NDC Juaben Constituency Secretary who had plans to contest in the NDC Juaben constituency chairmanship race. He said the party’s decision to initially support the headmaster followed a meeting at which he strongly denied the allegations and presented them as a politically motivated attempt to destroy his reputation. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, November 3, Mr Kwetey said the party had originally intended to ask the headmaster to step aside or withdraw, given the seriousness of the reports emerging about him. However, at a meeting on Monday, October 19, the party decided to hear his account before taking action, in keeping with what Mr Kwetey described as the need to give him a fair hearing. He said the headmaster’s emphatic denial, coupled with a report by the Ghana Education Service (GES) which had cleared him, influenced the party’s decision at the time. He said Mr Abdulai spoke with such conviction that party officials were persuaded that the allegations could have been part of a political plot against him. Documentary changed the party’s position. Mr Kwetey said, in hindsight, the party should have delayed its decision until it had watched the investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni, which was broadcast later that evening. He explained that the party was unaware that the documentary would be aired on the same day it met the headmaster and reached its initial position. “If we had heard about it, we would have said we pause that decision, watch that evidence properly,” he said. According to him, the documentary fundamentally altered the party’s understanding of the allegations and prompted a reassessment of the headmaster’s account. Mr Kwetey said he watched the documentary and subsequently spoke directly with Mr Awuni the following morning, after which the party concluded that the matter was far more serious than had been presented during its earlier engagement with the headmaster. He said the NDC consequently changed its position and directed Mr Abdulai to withdraw. “It appeared like a flip-flop only because we had not had full access to that documentary,” he explained. The General Secretary insisted that had the party seen the documentary before its October 19 meeting, it would have maintained its original position that the headmaster should step aside. ‘A lesson learned’ Mr Kwetey conceded that the party’s handling of the matter offered an important lesson about how it should respond to serious allegations, particularly where further evidence is expected to emerge. He said the party’s failure to consider the documentary before making its initial decision had affected its assessment of the case. The controversy centres on allegations of sexual abuse involving female students of Obuasi SHTS and the school’s headmaster. The allegations were brought into the public domain through an investigation by Mr Awuni, triggering public concern and calls for accountability. The headmaster was subsequently interdicted by the GES, while the police began investigating the allegations. Mr Kwetey’s comments represent an acknowledgement by the NDC that its initial assessment was made without access to evidence that later proved decisive in changing the party’s position.
